Dismissing all portal data would also be wrong. Check the actual result, current symptoms and responsibility for explaining the next step.
handover: Herr Reuter berichtet über einen im Portal erhöht markierten Calprotectinwert und Sorge vor Morbus Crohn. Der Wert ist im klinischen Zusammenhang zu beurteilen und stellt allein keine gesicherte Diagnose dar; die Befundbesprechung wird geklärt.
focus: Explain a nonspecific inflammation marker
topicTitle: Let's talk about the awkward bit

title: The allergy story interrupted by a phone
setting: Sara is describing a previous reaction after contrast material when the clinic phone rings.
hook: Sara is describing a previous reaction after contrast material when the clinic phone rings. She has mentioned breathing difficulty and emergency treatment, but the substance and timing remain unclear. When the call ends, the interview almost moves straight to her bowel symptoms. Sara holds an old hospital envelope that she has carried through three appointments; each time someone promised to look later. This time the task is to resume the unfinished safety-relevant story, verify what can be verified and make the uncertainty visible to the team.
question: Sara’s contrast-reaction history was interrupted by a call. What should you return to before planning?
options: Leave the envelope unread and record no known allergies
Resume and flag the reaction history before planning
Declare that she can never have any imaging
feedback: The correct move preserves and verifies the relevant history. Recording no allergies would directly contradict what Sara has reported. A blanket ban on all imaging is also unsupported. Clarify the event and communicate it to the responsible team, which can consider appropriate individual investigation choices and precautions.
handover: Frau Holm berichtet über Atemnot und notfallmäßige Behandlung nach früherer Kontrastmittelgabe. Präparat und genauer Verlauf sind noch unklar; der mitgebrachte Bericht wird geprüft und die Angabe vor weiterer Untersuchungsplanung hervorgehoben.
focus: Preserve a serious reaction history during interruptions
topicTitle: Let's talk about the awkward bit

title: The smallest parcel with the most questions
setting: Jette has been handed a stool sample container and a sheet full of tiny print.
hook: Jette has been handed a stool sample container and a sheet full of tiny print. She understands why a sample was requested but not where it should go afterward. Her first instinct is to post it, because every other complicated transaction in her life currently involves a parcel label. She laughs, then admits she was too embarrassed to ask at reception. You need to confirm the local instructions, explain them plainly and avoid inventing collection, storage or delivery rules that may differ for the requested test.
question: Jette does not know where to deliver her stool sample. What is the most useful response?
options: Invent a delivery deadline from memory
Tell her the leaflet makes questions unnecessary
Verify local instructions and check her understanding
feedback: Verifying the actual process makes the explanation reliable. Test-specific requirements should not be guessed. Dismissing questions because a leaflet exists confuses information delivery with understanding. Confirm the collection point and instructions, then ask Jette to describe the plan so any remaining uncertainty can be resolved before she leaves.
handover: Frau Hansen benötigt verständliche organisatorische Hinweise zur angeforderten Stuhlprobe. Die testspezifischen örtlichen Anweisungen werden überprüft und rückgefragt; eine erfolgte oder verwertbare Probenabgabe liegt noch nicht vor.
focus: Check practical specimen instructions respectfully
topicTitle: Let's talk about the awkward bit

title: The diary written at two in the morning
setting: Malik brings a diary of diarrhoea episodes.
hook: Malik brings a diary of diarrhoea episodes. Most entries are daytime, but two are written in a different pen because he recorded them at night beside his bed. He has been calling the problem a nervous stomach, and the referral repeats that phrase. His new diary may add detail that the label obscures. You need to ask whether symptoms woke him, what happened and how often, without suggesting an answer or declaring one particular disease from a pair of entries.
question: Malik’s diary has night entries. What should you clarify before interpreting them?
options: Clarify whether symptoms woke him and update the history
Copy nervous stomach without discussing the diary
Tell him night entries prove inflammatory bowel disease
feedback: The correct move retrieves a more precise history. Keeping the old label misses a possible change, while declaring a disease from the diary overstates the evidence. Ask neutral follow-up questions, document the report and leave diagnosis to assessment of the whole picture rather than one memorable detail.
handover: Herr Dorn berichtet anhand seines Tagebuchs über zweimaliges nächtliches Erwachen durch Stuhldrang. Häufigkeit und weiterer Verlauf werden konkretisiert; die frühere Bezeichnung als nervöser Magen erklärt die Beschwerden nicht abschließend.
focus: Ask about night symptoms without leading answers
topicTitle: Let's talk about the awkward bit

title: The sick note and the whole story
setting: Alina’s manager has asked why she repeatedly needs the toilet during shifts.
hook: Alina’s manager has asked why she repeatedly needs the toilet during shifts. She wants help explaining the disruption but does not want bowel symptoms discussed in the staff group chat. A colleague has already suggested an elaborate cover story involving a broken bus route, which would require its own spreadsheet. No diagnosis is yet confirmed. The consultation needs to identify what practical support she wants, which information she consents to share and how the responsible clinician can address documentation without inventing a diagnosis for convenience.
question: Alina wants work support without sharing her entire bowel history. What should be agreed first?
options: Send the manager the full bowel history
Agree the purpose and scope of any workplace communication
Invent a confirmed diagnosis to make the request stronger
feedback: The useful move establishes what help is needed and what may be shared. A full history is not automatically necessary for a practical request. Inventing a diagnosis creates false documentation. Discuss the wording and responsible process with Alina, preserving confidentiality while avoiding guarantees about an employer’s eventual response.
handover: Frau Maas wünscht Unterstützung bei der Kommunikation arbeitsbezogener Einschränkungen durch Darmbeschwerden. Eine Diagnose ist nicht gesichert; Zweck, Empfänger und Umfang einer möglichen Bescheinigung werden mit ihr abgestimmt.
focus: Separate workplace needs from confidential clinical details
topicTitle: Let's talk about the awkward bit

title: The old explanation needs a new check
setting: Henrik has had haemorrhoids before, so he filed new blood in his stool under an old explanation and carried on preparing a family reunion.
hook: Henrik has had haemorrhoids before, so he filed new blood in his stool under an old explanation and carried on preparing a family reunion. His spreadsheet contains seating positions for thirty people but no space for symptoms. Now he mentions that his bowel habit has also changed. No examination has established the source of bleeding. You need to respect his past experience while explaining why a familiar diagnosis does not automatically account for a new or changing pattern.
question: Henrik assumes new bleeding comes from old haemorrhoids. What should you do next?
options: Clarify the new pattern and arrange assessment
Assume the old haemorrhoids explain everything
Announce cancer because bleeding has recurred
feedback: The right move preserves both history and uncertainty. Automatically reusing the old explanation could miss a different cause. Announcing cancer would also exceed the evidence. Ask about present bleeding and associated changes, assess urgency and document what has actually been established rather than what feels most familiar.
handover: Herr Maas berichtet über erneute Blutbeimengungen im Stuhl und veränderte Stuhlgewohnheiten bei anamnestisch bekannten Hämorrhoiden. Die aktuelle Blutungsquelle ist nicht gesichert; Verlauf und Dringlichkeit werden klinisch beurteilt.
focus: Avoid attributing new bleeding to known haemorrhoids
topicTitle: The question nobody wants to ask

title: The calendar with two kinds of bad day
setting: Paula says she has constipation, then apologises because yesterday she had loose stool.
hook: Paula says she has constipation, then apologises because yesterday she had loose stool. She thinks the two statements cancel each other out. Her calendar uses circles and triangles for different days, making it resemble a secret weather forecast. The changes have lasted several weeks and are unlike her usual pattern. You need to help her describe sequence, frequency and associated symptoms without demanding one tidy word or treating alternating symptoms as proof of a particular diagnosis.
question: Paula thinks constipation and loose stool cancel each other out. How should you document the pattern?
options: Choose constipation and discard the loose stool
Record the sequence and change from usual habits
Say alternating stool proves a bowel tumour
feedback: Both parts belong in the account. Discarding one creates a cleaner but less accurate history, while declaring a tumour from the pattern overstates the evidence. Ask about associated changes and current severity, then document the timeline in ordinary language that the next clinician can interpret with examination and investigations.
handover: Frau Kern berichtet über seit mehreren Wochen wechselnde Obstipation und dünnen Stuhl, abweichend von ihren üblichen Stuhlgewohnheiten. Weitere Begleitsymptome und Ursache sind noch zu klären; eine konkrete Diagnose ist nicht gesichert.
focus: Clarify alternating bowel habits
topicTitle: The question nobody wants to ask

title: The family tree needs names, not guesses
setting: David says cancer runs in the family, but the details come from conversations at weddings.
hook: David says cancer runs in the family, but the details come from conversations at weddings. His uncle had “something in the stomach,” his father had a polyp removed, and a cousin says everyone should have the same operation. David is being assessed for a new bowel change, not attending a family debate. He has drawn a family tree whose arrows are more confident than its facts. You need to separate relatives, diagnoses and uncertain recollections without presenting a guessed inheritance pattern as established.
question: David’s family cancer history contains uncertain diagnoses. How should you clarify it?
options: Record hereditary cancer as confirmed
Ignore the entire history because some details are missing
Separate relatives and verified versus uncertain diagnoses
feedback: The correct move retains relevant information while showing its limits. A hereditary diagnosis cannot be confirmed from this account, but incomplete history should not be discarded. Clarify the relationships and diagnoses, seek records where feasible and leave the interpretation to assessment rather than the cousin’s confident recommendation.
handover: Herr Arendt berichtet über mögliche gastrointestinale Tumorerkrankungen in der Familie; beim Vater ist möglicherweise nur eine Polypektomie erfolgt. Betroffene Angehörige, Diagnosen und Erkrankungsalter werden getrennt erhoben, ein erbliches Syndrom ist nicht belegt.
focus: Clarify family history and uncertainty
topicTitle: The question nobody wants to ask

title: The examination with a pause button
setting: Leonie is told that a rectal examination may be part of assessing her symptoms.
hook: Leonie is told that a rectal examination may be part of assessing her symptoms. She goes quiet and folds the information leaflet into a precise square. She is not refusing, but she has not agreed either. A busy colleague mistakes the silence for permission and reaches for supplies. The learning task is to stop that assumption, explain the purpose and process in respectful language, offer appropriate support and make clear that Leonie can ask questions or ask for the examination to stop.
question: Leonie is silent before an intimate examination. What needs to happen before proceeding?
options: Explain, offer support and obtain consent before proceeding
Treat silence as agreement
Say routine examinations do not need discussion
feedback: The right move respects Leonie’s control and provides information before action. Silence does not establish consent, and calling an examination routine does not remove the need to explain it. Keep the language direct and respectful, offer appropriate support and make the option to stop clear throughout the process.
handover: Frau Weber hat Fragen zur vorgeschlagenen digital-rektalen Untersuchung bei Darmbeschwerden. Eine Einwilligung liegt noch nicht vor; Zweck, Ablauf, Begleitung und Möglichkeit zur Unterbrechung werden vorab besprochen.
focus: Seek consent for an intimate examination
topicTitle: The question nobody wants to ask

title: An urgent appointment is not a diagnosis
setting: Ralf receives an earlier specialist appointment than expected and concludes that someone must already know he has cancer.
hook: Ralf receives an earlier specialist appointment than expected and concludes that someone must already know he has cancer. His daughter has cleared the family calendar; he has quietly cancelled a fishing trip he had been planning for months. The referral is for assessment of symptoms, and no confirmed diagnosis appears in the available information. You need to explain why a prompt investigation can be appropriate while avoiding both the claim that cancer is established and the equally unsupported promise that it is impossible.
question: Ralf thinks a rapid referral proves a cancer diagnosis. What should you explain?
options: Confirm cancer from the appointment speed
Explain the referral’s purpose and diagnostic uncertainty
Promise urgent referrals always turn out harmless
feedback: The useful answer addresses the inference Ralf has made. Appointment timing alone proves neither cancer nor its absence. Avoid comforting him with another unsupported certainty. Review the letter, clarify the planned assessment and make the follow-up discussion visible so that uncertainty has a practical next step rather than an empty reassurance.
handover: Herr Henning interpretiert den zeitnahen Untersuchungstermin als Krebsdiagnose. Bisher ist keine Diagnose gesichert; Anlass und Ziel der beschleunigten Abklärung sowie die weitere Befundbesprechung werden erläutert.
focus: Explain referral urgency without false certainty
topicTitle: The question nobody wants to ask

title: The question she saved until the door
setting: Birgit asks sensible questions about appointments, then waits until your hand is on the door before asking whether she will need a stoma.
hook: Birgit asks sensible questions about appointments, then waits until your hand is on the door before asking whether she will need a stoma. Her neighbour’s experience has become the picture she sees whenever bowel investigations are mentioned. She has changed the subject twice because she does not know a comfortable word for it. No diagnosis or treatment plan is confirmed. You need to stop leaving, give the question proper space and explain the boundary between discussing a fear and predicting an operation.
question: Birgit asks about a possible stoma just as you are leaving. What response addresses her actual concern?
options: Promise she will never need a stoma
Say every bowel cancer operation requires one
Explore the fear and explain what is not yet known
feedback: The correct move makes room for the underlying concern while preserving uncertainty. Neither an absolute promise nor a sweeping statement about operations is justified. Clarify the term and her fear, explain that findings guide individual options, and ensure she knows where that discussion can continue if it becomes relevant.
handover: Frau Faber äußert Sorge vor einem möglichen Stoma nach Erfahrungen im Bekanntenkreis. Eine Diagnose und ein Operationsplan liegen noch nicht vor; die Befürchtung wird aufgegriffen, ohne die spätere Behandlung vorwegzunehmen.
focus: Elicit the feared consequence behind a procedure question
topicTitle: The question nobody wants to ask

title: The form can remain unfinished
setting: Samuel reports that bleeding from his bottom has not stopped and that he feels increasingly weak.
hook: Samuel reports that bleeding from his bottom has not stopped and that he feels increasingly weak. He is still trying to answer the admission questions because he assumes cooperation means finishing them. His partner searches for an insurance card while the history form remains open. The scene is deliberately simple: there is no need to establish the exact diagnosis before recognising the need for urgent clinical help. Your communication should release Samuel from the paperwork and make the current concern unmistakable to the team.
question: Samuel reports ongoing bleeding and increasing weakness. What takes priority now?
options: Call the clinical team immediately and stop routine questions
Finish insurance details before calling
Assume the bleeding comes from known haemorrhoids
feedback: Ongoing heavy bleeding with weakness requires urgent assessment. Administrative completion would delay help, and assuming a benign source would be unsafe. Communicate the current report, observed condition if available and missing measurements. Keep the diagnosis uncertain while being decisive about the need for immediate clinical involvement.
handover: Herr Falk berichtet über anhaltende rektale Blutung und zunehmende Schwäche. Das Routinegespräch wird sofort unterbrochen und das Behandlungsteam alarmiert; Blutungsquelle und aktuelle Vitalparameter sind noch nicht bekannt.
focus: Prioritise ongoing heavy bleeding over routine history
topicTitle: The question nobody wants to ask

title: The symptom nobody actually asked about
setting: Yasmin reads her draft summary and notices “no weight change.” Nobody asked her about weight.
hook: Yasmin reads her draft summary and notices “no weight change.” Nobody asked her about weight. She has been buying looser clothes but has not used a scale, and she assumed the clinician would ask if it mattered. The phrase came from a template, not from her account. A tempting response is to dismiss it as standard wording. The better task is to correct the record and ask a neutral question, without replacing one invented fact with a new measured weight loss that also has no evidence.
question: Yasmin finds an unasked negative in her draft summary. How should you repair it?
options: Keep the phrase because it is standard wording
Correct the unsupported negative and ask neutrally
Replace it with a precise weight loss without measuring
feedback: The right move repairs both the wording and the information gap. Standard templates do not authorise invented negatives. An exact weight loss would be equally unsupported without a source. Record the reported change and uncertainty, then review whether other unchecked template statements have entered the draft.
handover: Frau Stein weist darauf hin, dass eine Gewichtsveränderung nicht erfragt wurde, obwohl der Entwurf sie verneint. Sie berichtet über veränderten Kleidungssitz ohne Messwerte; die Dokumentation wird korrigiert und der Zeitraum geklärt.
focus: Remove invented negative findings
topicTitle: The question nobody wants to ask

title: The cardigan in the warm office
setting: Frederik wears a cardigan in an office where everyone else argues about opening windows.
hook: Frederik wears a cardigan in an office where everyone else argues about opening windows. He has been tired for months, struggles to concentrate and says his family calls him lazy. His calendar is full of caring responsibilities, so he has accepted the description himself. A colleague finally encouraged him to seek assessment. The cardigan is a memorable detail, not a diagnosis. You need to hear the changes in energy, temperature tolerance and daily functioning without reducing the person to either a personality judgment or a thyroid label.
question: Frederik calls himself lazy while describing months of fatigue and cold sensitivity. How should you respond?
options: Explore the change and avoid character judgments
Agree he needs more willpower
Confirm thyroid disease from the cardigan
feedback: The useful response opens the history and recognises the change. Calling it laziness dismisses symptoms, while diagnosing from one memorable detail overstates the evidence. Ask about the full pattern and practical burden, then explain the next assessment step without treating the person’s clothing or family label as a clinical result.
handover: Herr Blum berichtet über seit Monaten zunehmende Müdigkeit, Konzentrationsprobleme und vermehrtes Frieren. Eine Schilddrüsenfunktionsstörung ist eine mögliche Erklärung, jedoch bisher nicht gesichert; weitere Anamnese und Befunde stehen aus.
focus: Explore a cluster without calling it laziness

title: The till is not the only thing racing
setting: Nadine works at a busy shop and describes trembling hands, feeling unusually warm and a racing heartbeat.
hook: Nadine works at a busy shop and describes trembling hands, feeling unusually warm and a racing heartbeat. She has been told that retail makes everyone nervous, which is true about the queue but not a complete explanation of her symptoms. She is worried that asking again will make her seem difficult. The duration and current severity still need clarification. You need to take the physical account seriously, assess whether immediate review is needed and keep psychological and physical possibilities open rather than choosing one from her job title.
question: Nadine’s shaking and palpitations have been called only anxiety. What should the next assessment establish?
options: Attribute everything to her busy job
Assess the current symptoms and keep causes open
Write measured tachycardia without checking a pulse
feedback: The right move takes the report seriously and establishes current urgency. A demanding job does not prove a cause. Palpitations and a measured fast heart rate are related but not interchangeable facts. Ask relevant questions, obtain clinical assessment and avoid replacing one premature label with another.
handover: Frau Kühn berichtet über Palpitationen, Händezittern und Wärmeempfindlichkeit. Aktuelle Ausprägung, Begleitsymptome und gemessene Herzfrequenz sind noch unbekannt; eine ausschließliche Stressursache oder Hyperthyreose ist nicht belegt.
focus: Avoid labelling physical symptoms as anxiety alone

title: Three letters and a very large worry
setting: Bastian brings a laboratory printout covered with question marks around TSH.
hook: Bastian brings a laboratory printout covered with question marks around TSH. He thought the larger number meant his thyroid must be working harder, then found an explanation saying the opposite can happen. He has been tired and wants a sentence he can remember without learning endocrinology overnight. No individual interpretation is supplied in this scene. Your task is to explain that TSH is a signal involved in controlling the thyroid and that the clinician interprets it with thyroid hormone results and the clinical context.
question: Bastian mistakes TSH for the thyroid hormone itself. What explanation is most useful?
options: Diagnose from TSH alone without context
Read every abbreviation without checking understanding
Explain the signal distinction and arrange individual interpretation
feedback: The correct move teaches enough to make the result discussion understandable. One value should not be treated as the whole clinical picture. A list of abbreviations may increase confusion. Use plain language, check the distinction and make clear which parts of Bastian’s individual result still need professional interpretation.
handover: Herr Reim fragt nach der Bedeutung von TSH bei Müdigkeit und vorliegenden Laborunterlagen. Die individuelle Befundkonstellation ist in diesem Gespräch nicht interpretiert; Steuersignal und Schilddrüsenhormone werden sprachlich unterschieden.
focus: Explain TSH versus thyroid hormones simply

title: The tablet that meets the morning chaos
setting: Carla has prescribed thyroid medicine but cannot explain her current routine confidently.
hook: Carla has prescribed thyroid medicine but cannot explain her current routine confidently. Some mornings she leaves early, some mornings she cares for her father, and on others the dog wins the race to the front door. She worries that admitting missed or changed timing will earn a reprimand. You have not verified the prescription or recent monitoring. The scene is about discovering the actual routine and barriers, then obtaining individual advice, rather than changing doses or treating imperfect recall as deliberate noncooperation.
question: Carla cannot reliably recall her thyroid tablet routine. What should you do before any treatment change?
options: Verify the routine and seek individual advice
Tell her to double the next dose whenever unsure
Record perfect adherence because she has a prescription
feedback: The useful move identifies what actually happens and who can advise safely. A prescription does not prove regular use. A universal catch-up instruction may be inappropriate and should not be improvised. Thank Carla for the information, verify the plan and agree a practical support step without altering treatment in this exercise.
handover: Frau Meier berichtet über Unsicherheit bei der regelmäßigen Einnahme ihrer Schilddrüsenmedikation. Präparat, verordneter Plan und tatsächliche Einnahme werden verifiziert; eine Dosisänderung wird aus der unvollständigen Anamnese nicht abgeleitet.
focus: Explore medicine routines without blame or dose changes

title: The mirror found a question
setting: Lukas noticed a change at the front of his neck while practising a presentation in the mirror.
hook: Lukas noticed a change at the front of his neck while practising a presentation in the mirror. The presentation survived; his attention did not. He has read the word Struma and assumes it is a type of cancer. The swelling has not yet been clinically characterised in this scene. Your role is to explain what the term describes, ask about the change and relevant symptoms, and help him understand why an assessment is needed without offering an unsupported guarantee about the cause.
question: Lukas thinks Struma means cancer. What should you explain and assess?
options: Confirm cancer because the neck looks enlarged
Translate the term and assess the change
Promise every thyroid enlargement is harmless
feedback: The correct explanation separates enlargement from its possible causes. Neither cancer nor a harmless condition can be established from the term alone. Ask about the timeline and associated changes, including features that might alter urgency, and ensure the next assessment step is clear rather than relying on reassurance about vocabulary.
handover: Herr Ebert berichtet über eine neu bemerkte Veränderung am vorderen Hals und Sorge wegen des Begriffs Struma. Ausmaß, Ursache und Begleitsymptome sind noch zu beurteilen; eine maligne Erkrankung ist damit weder bestätigt noch ausgeschlossen.
focus: Explain enlargement without equating it with malignancy

title: Her tiredness keeps losing the appointment
setting: Petra spends the first five minutes describing her son’s appointments.
hook: Petra spends the first five minutes describing her son’s appointments. When you ask about her own fatigue, she says his needs are more important and reaches for the family calendar. It is impressively organised, except there is no box for her. She reports months of slowing down and difficulty concentrating, but neither the physical nor emotional contribution has been assessed. You need to make space for her symptoms and practical constraints, without deciding that caregiving alone explains everything or treating the family context as irrelevant.
question: Petra keeps replacing her own fatigue story with her son’s appointments. How should you make room for her?
options: Explain the fatigue entirely by caregiving
Ignore the family calendar and prescribe an impossible schedule
Explore her symptoms and make follow-up practical
feedback: The useful move protects both clinical attention and feasibility. Caregiving pressure is relevant but does not rule out other causes. A plan that ignores her constraints may fail before assessment happens. Hear her symptoms, clarify what is unknown and coordinate a realistic next step without promising the cause from the social history.
handover: Frau Lenz berichtet über monatelange Müdigkeit und verlangsamte Alltagsbewältigung bei hoher familiärer Pflegebelastung. Die Ursache ist offen; eigene Beschwerden und organisatorische Möglichkeiten für die weitere Abklärung werden gezielt erhoben.
focus: Include caregiving burden without explaining away symptoms

title: A picture cannot answer every question
setting: Anton has been scheduled for thyroid investigations and believes an ultrasound will show whether every area is “hot” or “cold.” He has used the same words to describe the waiting room radiators, which has made the discussion unexpectedly confusing.
hook: Anton has been scheduled for thyroid investigations and believes an ultrasound will show whether every area is “hot” or “cold.” He has used the same words to describe the waiting room radiators, which has made the discussion unexpectedly confusing. The specialist plan is not yet verified. You need to explain that different investigations answer different questions about structure and activity, while avoiding a recommendation that he must have every available test or a claim that a reassuring image settles hormone function.
question: Anton expects ultrasound to answer every thyroid function question. What distinction should you explain?
options: Explain the different questions and verify the individual plan
Say ultrasound measures all thyroid function
Book every test because each gives different information
feedback: The correct move distinguishes purpose without expanding the plan unnecessarily. Ultrasound should not be described as answering every functional question. Different capabilities do not make all tests automatically appropriate. Verify the specialist plan and invite Anton to explain the distinction back before discussing any individual next step.
handover: Herr Kranz fragt nach der funktionellen Einordnung eines möglichen Schilddrüsenknotens im Ultraschall. Struktur- und Funktionsdiagnostik werden unterschieden; konkrete Befunde und die individuell vorgesehene Untersuchungsfolge sind noch zu bestätigen.
focus: Distinguish structure from function in thyroid tests

title: Three options and one real life
setting: Maren has been told that different treatments may be discussed for an overactive thyroid.
hook: Maren has been told that different treatments may be discussed for an overactive thyroid. She wants to know which is best, but best for her includes caring for an elderly parent, travelling for work and how much monitoring she can manage. She has made a comparison chart with three columns and no facts in them yet. You are helping her prepare for the specialist discussion, not selecting a treatment. The task is to elicit priorities and questions without presenting every option as equivalent or automatically suitable.
question: Maren asks which thyroid treatment is best for her life. How can you prepare a useful specialist discussion?
options: Pick the easiest-sounding treatment immediately
Elicit priorities and prepare questions for individual advice
Say her daily life should not affect discussion
feedback: The correct move supports a shared discussion while preserving the clinician’s role in assessing suitability. Choosing from a generic list would skip essential facts. Excluding daily life would miss treatment burdens that matter to Maren. Gather her priorities and questions, then connect them to a verified specialist explanation.
handover: Frau Voigt möchte mögliche Behandlungsoptionen einer berichteten Hyperthyreose hinsichtlich Alltag und Betreuungspflichten verstehen. Individuelle Eignung, Nutzen und Risiken der Optionen sind im Fachgespräch zu klären; eine Therapieentscheidung wird hier nicht vorweggenommen.
focus: Prepare shared decision questions without choosing treatment

title: The interview is not the priority
setting: Erik arrives sweating and shaking after a bicycle ride.
hook: Erik arrives sweating and shaking after a bicycle ride. He says he used insulin but missed breakfast. The story is not yet complete, and no glucose value has been provided. A trainee begins asking about remote operations because that is the next box on the form. Erik is finding it harder to follow the questions. This is the moment to stop the routine interview, summon the clinical team and communicate the possible acute problem without waiting to identify the exact insulin product or finish the social history.
question: Erik is sweating, shaking and struggling to concentrate after insulin without breakfast. What happens first?
options: Stop routine questions and summon immediate assessment
Finish the full medication history before seeking help
Assume water and a rest have solved the problem
feedback: The current symptoms and reduced concentration require prompt clinical attention. Completing the routine history first would delay that response. A pause or drink of water does not establish recovery. Communicate the suspected issue and missing glucose measurement, while allowing the clinical team to assess and manage the person directly.
handover: Herr Brandt berichtet über Insulingabe ohne Frühstück und zeigt Schwitzen sowie Zittern; er gibt Konzentrationsprobleme an. Bei möglicher Hypoglykämie wird sofort das Behandlungsteam hinzugezogen, ein aktueller Glukosewert liegt noch nicht vor.
focus: Recognise a possible acute low-glucose episode

title: Two pens, one uncertain answer
setting: At a follow-up after an assessed episode, Selin brings two insulin pens and a photograph of a third package.
hook: At a follow-up after an assessed episode, Selin brings two insulin pens and a photograph of a third package. She calls them the blue one and the evening one, but the labels and her routine have not yet been reconciled. She is trying hard to remember and becomes more confident whenever you suggest a name. Her handbag is organised enough to contain spare batteries for a torch she no longer owns. You need accurate identification, not a fluent guess produced by leading questions.
question: Selin identifies insulin by pen colour and agrees with suggested names. How should you verify the history?
options: Identify the insulin from pen colour alone
Verify labels and actual use without leading prompts
Choose the name she agrees with most quickly
feedback: The right move separates verified product information from uncertain recall. Colour alone is not a reliable prescription, and rapid agreement may reflect prompting rather than memory. Use the label, plan and prescribing service where needed, then check Selin’s understanding of the clarified individual instructions without inventing a new regimen.
handover: Frau Kramer ist nach einem abgeklärten Ereignis zur Nachbesprechung erschienen und kann ihre Insulinpräparate nicht sicher benennen. Etiketten, Verordnungsplan und tatsächliche Anwendung werden abgeglichen; unklare Angaben bleiben als solche gekennzeichnet.
focus: Identify insulin without relying on colour

title: The lunch break that kept moving
setting: Jan is attending a planned review after the acute team assessed a suspected low-glucose episode.
hook: Jan is attending a planned review after the acute team assessed a suspected low-glucose episode. His work rota calls lunch flexible, which in practice means it moves whenever a delivery arrives. He had been trying to follow his diabetes plan around a schedule that behaves like a weather forecast. You are not changing medication in this exercise. The communication goal is to reconstruct what happened, identify the practical mismatch and prepare an individual discussion with the diabetes team without blaming Jan for having a complicated working day.
question: Jan’s meal breaks move unpredictably. What should the follow-up conversation establish?
options: Blame him for not following an ideal schedule
Change his insulin plan without verification
Reconstruct the day and identify barriers for individual review
feedback: The useful move produces a realistic account for the diabetes team. Blame can hide the very obstacle that needs solving. Unverified treatment changes are outside this communication task. Distinguish the reported timing from confirmed records and help Jan ask for advice that fits his work rather than a fictional perfect day.
handover: Herr Vetter berichtet in der Nachbesprechung über unvorhersehbare Essenspausen im Schichtdienst. Der Ablauf von Nahrungsaufnahme, Aktivität und Medikation wird rekonstruiert und dem Diabetesteam zur individuellen Beratung übergeben; die Ursache des Ereignisses wird nicht allein daraus abgeleitet.
focus: Explore a real-world prevention barrier after assessment

title: No drink during reduced consciousness
setting: Katrin becomes unresponsive while waiting for assessment after reporting shaking and sweating.
hook: Katrin becomes unresponsive while waiting for assessment after reporting shaking and sweating. A companion reaches for a drink because he remembers that sugar can help some low-glucose episodes. There is no current glucose measurement or confirmed diagnosis in the scene. You must stop the routine interaction, summon the emergency clinical team and prevent an oral drink being given to someone who is not safely responsive. The communication should be direct and calm, with no attempt to finish the history or make light of the situation.
question: Katrin is unresponsive and a companion offers a drink. What should you communicate immediately?
options: Alert the emergency team and prevent oral intake
Give a drink before calling the team
Wait for a full medication list before escalating
feedback: The correct move prioritises the emergency and avoids giving oral intake to an unresponsive person. A drink can be unsafe in that state, and medication verification must not delay help. Describe the observed responsiveness and preceding reported symptoms, leaving the cause and treatment to the responding clinical team.
handover: Frau Fuchs reagiert aktuell nicht ausreichend; zuvor wurden Schwitzen und Zittern berichtet. Das Notfallteam wird sofort alarmiert und eine orale Gabe durch die Begleitperson unterbunden; Glukosewert und Ursache sind noch unbekannt.
focus: Communicate safe escalation when responsiveness deteriorates

title: The friend remembers a different minute
setting: During follow-up after an acute assessment, Mika remembers becoming shaky after the cycle café.
hook: During follow-up after an acute assessment, Mika remembers becoming shaky after the cycle café. His friend remembers the shaking before they stopped. Both are trying to help, and the café receipt establishes when they paid, not when symptoms started. The two accounts do not need a winner; they need attribution. You are reconstructing the event for the team, including food, exertion and reported symptoms, without merging the accounts into a precise chronology nobody can support.
question: Mika and his friend disagree about onset relative to a café stop. How should you record the accounts?
options: Force them to agree before documenting anything
Attribute both accounts and preserve timing uncertainty
Use the receipt as the exact symptom-onset time
feedback: The useful response keeps the evidence traceable. Forced agreement can hide genuine uncertainty, while the receipt only records a transaction. Ask what was directly observed and what was inferred, then document both accounts. The goal is a reliable reconstruction for assessment, not a perfectly smooth story at any cost.
handover: Herr Stern und seine Begleitperson schildern den Symptombeginn zeitlich unterschiedlich. Beide Angaben werden mit Einverständnis getrennt dokumentiert; der Kassenbeleg belegt nur den Zahlungszeitpunkt, nicht den genauen Beginn des Ereignisses.
focus: Keep patient and witness accounts distinct

title: The word noncompliant closes the door
setting: Derya is attending a diabetes review after an episode that worried her.
hook: Derya is attending a diabetes review after an episode that worried her. She hesitates when asked about meals because a previous note called her noncompliant. She has been skipping lunch to make money last until payday and does not want this discussed in front of her colleague, who gave her a lift. Her phone contains a careful grocery list, not a lack of interest in health. The task is to create private space and identify support needs without reducing the problem to a character flaw.
question: Derya reveals privately that money sometimes does not cover lunch. How should the discussion proceed?
options: Repeat the noncompliant label
Discuss her finances openly with the colleague
Offer private discussion and identify practical support
feedback: The correct move makes disclosure safer and identifies a barrier that can affect care. A moral label adds little useful information. Sharing financial details without agreement breaches the intended privacy of the conversation. Clarify the routine, seek appropriate support and coordinate individual advice rather than issuing an improvised treatment change.
handover: Frau Koch berichtet im vertraulichen Gespräch über finanziell bedingte ausgelassene Mahlzeiten. Die Auswirkungen auf ihren Diabetesalltag und mögliche Unterstützung werden mit ihr abgestimmt; Informationen werden nicht ohne abgestimmten Umfang an die Begleitperson weitergegeben.
focus: Invite disclosure about missed meals without judgment

title: The emergency card nobody could explain
setting: Hugo and his partner bring an emergency card to a scheduled review.
hook: Hugo and his partner bring an emergency card to a scheduled review. The card is current according to their diabetes service, but neither can explain which part applies when Hugo is alert and which part applies when he is not responding normally. They have preserved the laminate beautifully; the meaning has not survived as well. Your role is to review the verified plan with the responsible team, check understanding and identify training needs, rather than invent a new universal set of treatment instructions.
question: Hugo carries an emergency card but cannot explain its instructions. What should the review check?
options: Review the verified plan and check each person’s understanding
Assume carrying the card proves readiness
Write a new medication rescue plan from memory
feedback: The useful move turns the existing plan into usable understanding with appropriate professional support. Carrying a card alone does not show that the instructions are clear. An improvised rescue regimen could be wrong. Confirm the current plan, practise explaining the relevant actions and arrange formal training where the team identifies a need.
handover: Herr Lind und seine Partnerin können Teile des vorliegenden Diabetes-Notfallplans nicht sicher erklären. Der aktuelle Plan wird mit dem zuständigen Team überprüft und rückgefragt; ein Schulungsbedarf, insbesondere bei Bewusstseinsstörung, wird geklärt.
focus: Check understanding of an existing individual plan

title: Today and the last few months are different questions
setting: Mona holds a recent HbA1c report and thinks it means today’s shaking cannot be related to low glucose.
hook: Mona holds a recent HbA1c report and thinks it means today’s shaking cannot be related to low glucose. She has developed the symptoms in the clinic, and the current glucose has not been checked. The printed result feels more solid than a new symptom because it has a date, a number and an official logo. Your immediate job is to obtain clinical assessment now. The later teaching point is that a longer-term marker and a current measurement answer different questions; one must not delay the other.
question: Mona uses an earlier HbA1c to dismiss current shaking. What takes priority now?
options: Use the previous HbA1c to rule out a current low
Obtain current assessment rather than relying on HbA1c
Finish a long explanation before calling the team
feedback: The correct move matches the immediate concern with immediate assessment. HbA1c reflects a longer period and cannot establish the current glucose level. A lengthy explanation would also delay help. State the distinction briefly, summon the team and return to the teaching discussion once the acute situation has been assessed.
handover: Frau Fiedler berichtet aktuell über Zittern und verweist auf einen früheren HbA1c-Befund. Ein aktueller Glukosewert liegt nicht vor; das Behandlungsteam wird sofort zur Beurteilung hinzugezogen, da der Langzeitwert die akute Situation nicht klärt.
focus: Distinguish current glucose from HbA1c

title: The collar has not shrunk
setting: Otto has stopped fastening the top button of his favourite shirt.
hook: Otto has stopped fastening the top button of his favourite shirt. He first blamed the laundry, an institution he already distrusts over missing socks. Now he can feel a painless lump in his neck and wants to know whether the absence of pain means it is harmless. The swelling has not been examined in this scene. You need to ask about onset, change and associated symptoms while explaining that pain is only one part of the account, not a reliable guarantee about the cause.
question: Otto thinks a painless neck lump must be harmless. How should you respond?
options: Assess the swelling and explain that painlessness is not a diagnosis
Reassure solely because the lump is painless
Name lymphoma and its stage from the collar story
feedback: The useful move takes the change seriously while keeping the cause open. Painlessness does not establish a harmless finding. Equally, the story does not confirm lymphoma or its extent. Clarify the history, obtain examination and preserve the difference between the patient’s observation and a verified clinical finding.
handover: Herr Bergmann berichtet über seit etwa zwei Wochen bemerkte schmerzlose Halsschwellung und enger sitzenden Hemdkragen. Ein Untersuchungsbefund und die Ursache liegen noch nicht vor; eine Lymphomerkrankung ist nicht gesichert.
focus: Explore painless swelling without minimising it

title: The laundry basket has become a diary
setting: Greta says she sweats at night, but she is unsure what counts as medically important.
hook: Greta says she sweats at night, but she is unsure what counts as medically important. She has changed nightclothes on several nights and wonders whether the new duvet is simply overqualified. She also reports a neck swelling that needs assessment. No measured temperature or weight record is provided. You need to ask what actually happens and when, not supply a dramatic description for her to agree with or turn a symptom cluster into an established cancer stage.
question: Greta is unsure whether her night sweating counts. What description should you obtain?
options: Prompt her to agree she has every textbook symptom
Ask for concrete details and distinguish measurements from impressions
Assign lymphoma stage from night sweats alone
feedback: The right move produces a usable description rather than an endorsed checklist. Leading questions can manufacture an apparently complete pattern. Staging cannot be inferred from night sweats alone. Document what Greta reports, identify measurements that are unavailable and let examination and further assessment determine how the information fits together.
handover: Frau Hesse berichtet über wiederholten nächtlichen Wechsel des Nachthemds und eine Halsschwellung. Gemessene Temperaturen und verlässliche Gewichtsangaben liegen noch nicht vor; die Symptomatik erlaubt keine Stadieneinteilung.
focus: Clarify night sweats without leading the description

title: The bruises without a furniture explanation
setting: Amira has noticed bruises she cannot connect to a bump and bleeding gums when brushing.
hook: Amira has noticed bruises she cannot connect to a bump and bleeding gums when brushing. She has also felt unusually tired. She jokes that her furniture would usually have a convincing case against her shins, but this time she cannot explain the marks. A friend has already named a blood cancer after seeing a photograph. The task is to obtain a careful bleeding and medication history, assess the current situation and explain why investigation matters without confirming the friend’s diagnosis or dismissing the pattern as ordinary clumsiness.
question: Amira reports unexplained bruises and gum bleeding. What should you do without confirming her friend’s diagnosis?
options: Confirm leukaemia from the photograph
Dismiss the bruises because she is young
Clarify bleeding history and arrange prompt assessment
feedback: The useful response gathers relevant details and obtains assessment. A photograph and symptom report do not establish a specific blood disease. Age is not a reason to ignore unexplained bleeding. Ask about the current condition and other relevant facts, escalating if needed, while keeping the diagnosis explicitly unconfirmed.
handover: Frau Frank berichtet über neu aufgetretene, nicht erklärte Hämatome, vermehrtes Zahnfleischbluten und Müdigkeit. Eine zeitnahe klinische Abklärung wird veranlasst; Blutbild, Untersuchungsbefund und Ursache sind bislang nicht bekannt.
focus: Take bleeding symptoms seriously without alarmist diagnosis

title: A sample is a question, not a verdict
setting: Timo hears that the specialist may recommend a tissue sample from a lymph node.
hook: Timo hears that the specialist may recommend a tissue sample from a lymph node. He interprets the word biopsy as confirmation that cancer has already been found. He has packed a hospital bag and included three chargers because uncertainty is easier to organise when it has a cable. No biopsy has been performed in this scene. You need to explain the purpose of sampling, distinguish a proposed investigation from a result and leave individual details of the procedure to the responsible team’s consent discussion.
question: Timo thinks a proposed biopsy means cancer is already confirmed. What should you explain?
options: Explain the purpose and confirm the individual proposal
Treat the proposed biopsy as a cancer diagnosis
Promise that the sample will certainly be benign
feedback: The correct move keeps the investigation and diagnosis separate. A proposal to obtain tissue does not supply a result, and a benign guarantee is equally unsupported. Clarify the actual procedure and arrange the appropriate consent conversation so Timo can ask informed questions about what is planned and why.
handover: Herr Weiß versteht die vorgeschlagene Lymphknotenbiopsie als bereits gesicherte Krebsdiagnose. Eine histologische Untersuchung ist noch nicht erfolgt; Zweck und individueller Vorschlag müssen im verantwortlichen Fachgespräch erläutert werden.
focus: Explain why tissue sampling may be proposed

title: The nephew with the appointment folder
setting: Hedwig’s nephew manages transport and has brought a beautifully indexed appointment folder.
hook: Hedwig’s nephew manages transport and has brought a beautifully indexed appointment folder. He also answers questions about her appetite before she has time to speak. Hedwig wants his support but quietly corrects him: she has been eating less than he thinks because he only sees her at Sunday lunch. The assessment concerns fatigue and a reported swelling. You need to welcome useful collateral information while checking her wishes and preserving the difference between what she experiences and what her nephew has directly observed.
question: Hedwig wants her nephew present but his appetite account differs from hers. How should you hear both?
options: Use the nephew’s answer as the whole appetite history
Hear her account first and attribute the nephew’s observations
Send him away despite her wish that he remain
feedback: The useful response respects Hedwig’s preference and improves the information. Her nephew’s involvement is welcome but not a substitute for her own account. Removing him automatically would also ignore her choice. Separate what each person knows and confirm any private or shared discussion boundaries as the consultation continues.
handover: Frau Reuter wünscht die Anwesenheit ihres Neffen und berichtet über geringere Nahrungsaufnahme außerhalb gemeinsamer Sonntagsmahlzeiten. Eigen- und Fremdanamnese werden getrennt erhoben; der Neffe kann den gesamten Wochenverlauf nicht direkt beurteilen.
focus: Preserve patient voice with a helpful relative

title: The blank stage box stays blank
setting: A colleague asks you to include a lymphoma stage in Kurt’s handover because the template has an empty box.
hook: A colleague asks you to include a lymphoma stage in Kurt’s handover because the template has an empty box. Kurt has reported a neck swelling and night sweats, but a diagnosis and extent of disease have not been established. The pressure is subtle: a filled box looks professional, a blank one looks unfinished. This case asks you to be professionally unfinished in the right way. State the available facts, the concern and the pending assessment rather than making the record look complete by inventing a stage.
question: Kurt’s template has an empty lymphoma-stage box but no confirmed diagnosis. What belongs there?
options: Guess the earliest stage because one swelling was mentioned
Fill a stage to avoid an incomplete-looking form
State that diagnosis and stage are not yet established
feedback: The right move makes the evidence boundary visible. One reported swelling does not establish the full distribution of disease or even confirm lymphoma. Filling a box for appearance can mislead later decisions and the patient. Record the known symptoms, unknown findings and pending assessment instead of manufacturing completeness.
handover: Herr Möller berichtet über Halsschwellung und Nachtschweiß. Weder eine Lymphomdiagnose noch eine Stadieneinteilung ist gesichert; im Übergabebrief werden diese Punkte ausdrücklich als noch ungeklärt ausgewiesen.
focus: Decline unsupported staging in professional handover

title: A serious possibility deserves a chair
setting: Sina has been asked to stay for a discussion after an initial assessment of fatigue and bruising.
hook: Sina has been asked to stay for a discussion after an initial assessment of fatigue and bruising. She hears the word leukaemia in a corridor conversation and assumes the whole team knows a diagnosis nobody will tell her. No confirmed result is supplied in this exercise. She is trying to remain composed while deciding whether to call her partner. Your task is to move the discussion into a private setting, establish what she heard and ensure the responsible clinician explains the actual evidence and uncertainty without speculation.
question: Sina overheard leukaemia in a corridor. How should you arrange the next conversation?
options: Arrange a private evidence-based discussion with her chosen support
Confirm the overheard word as her diagnosis
Deny any concern without checking the findings
feedback: The useful move repairs both setting and information. Overheard terminology is not enough to establish a diagnosis. An unverified denial may also be misleading. Check the actual findings, involve the clinician responsible for them and give Sina a choice about support while explaining what is known and what remains uncertain.
handover: Frau Beck ist stark verunsichert, nachdem sie auf dem Flur das Wort Leukämie gehört hat. Gesicherte Befunde sind in diesem Gespräch nicht verfügbar; eine vertrauliche Aufklärung durch das zuständige Team und gewünschte Begleitung werden organisiert.
focus: Communicate concern without a corridor announcement

title: The internet checklist keeps growing
setting: Vera arrives with twenty-seven questions after searching fatigue, itching and swollen glands.
hook: Vera arrives with twenty-seven questions after searching fatigue, itching and swollen glands. She has highlighted so much of the printout that the unmarked words now look suspicious. Some concerns relate to her actual symptoms; others come from lists she has read. No diagnosis is established. You need to agree priorities, separate experienced symptoms from feared possibilities and preserve questions for follow-up. The goal is a focused consultation that still feels heard, not a contest between the clock and the patient’s internet folder.
question: Vera’s internet list mixes symptoms she has with symptoms she fears. How should you organise the interview?
options: Record every highlighted symptom as present
Separate experienced symptoms from worries and agree priorities
Throw away the list and refuse to discuss it
feedback: The correct move makes the consultation manageable while preserving trust. Highlighting does not mean a symptom is present, so copying the list would create false findings. Rejecting the folder dismisses Vera’s effort and concern. Agree priorities, ask concrete questions and make follow-up for unresolved concerns explicit.
handover: Frau Nowak berichtet selbst über Müdigkeit und Juckreiz; weitere Punkte ihrer Internetliste beschreiben überwiegend Befürchtungen. Erlebte Symptome und Sorgen werden getrennt dokumentiert, Verlauf und Ursache sind noch abzuklären.
focus: Structure a long concern list without dismissing it

title: The familiar label does not protect this headache
setting: Nele has a history of migraine, but today’s headache began abruptly and was extremely severe almost immediately.
hook: Nele has a history of migraine, but today’s headache began abruptly and was extremely severe almost immediately. She says it is different from her usual episodes. The referral heading still says migraine, and a trainee starts asking about her usual triggers. No current neurological assessment has been performed. The task is to recognise that the new description changes the priority: stop the routine interview and obtain emergency clinical assessment, rather than allowing a familiar label to make an unfamiliar event sound safe.
question: Nele’s headache is suddenly extreme and unlike her usual migraine. What should happen first?
options: Escalate the sudden different headache immediately
Treat it as usual migraine because that is on the referral
Finish the trigger diary before seeking assessment
feedback: The correct move responds to the new warning pattern. A previous migraine diagnosis does not establish that this episode has the same cause. Routine diary questions would delay assessment. State the reported sudden onset and unusual severity, avoid invented examination findings and obtain urgent clinical help without diagnostic overconfidence.
handover: Frau Forster berichtet über plötzlich einsetzende, unmittelbar sehr starke und gegenüber bekannten Migräneepisoden deutlich veränderte Kopfschmerzen. Das Notfallteam wird sofort hinzugezogen; neurologische Befunde und Ursache sind noch unbekannt.
focus: Escalate sudden severe headache despite migraine history
topicTitle: A headache is not a whole history

title: The room is asking too many questions
setting: Finn is attending assessment of recurrent headaches and keeps turning away from the bright ceiling light.
hook: Finn is attending assessment of recurrent headaches and keeps turning away from the bright ceiling light. The computer beeps whenever a new task appears, as if it too wants a turn in the consultation. He can answer, but long compound questions make him lose track. No conclusion about the current episode has been established. You need to assess the situation appropriately while reducing avoidable sensory strain, using short questions and checking whether the environment is making communication unnecessarily difficult.
question: Finn struggles with light, noise and long questions. How should you adapt the interview?
options: Repeat long questions more loudly
Reduce avoidable strain and ask concise questions
Assume light sensitivity confirms migraine without assessment
feedback: The useful move makes the interview more accessible while preserving clinical attention. Louder or longer questions increase the burden. Light sensitivity alone does not establish a diagnosis. Ask about the current pattern and relevant changes, adapt the environment as possible and explain what must happen next in manageable steps.
handover: Herr Berger berichtet über Kopfschmerzen mit störender Lichtempfindlichkeit und erschwerter Konzentration im hellen Raum. Die Gesprächsbedingungen werden angepasst; die aktuelle Episode und mögliche Veränderungen müssen weiterhin klinisch beurteilt werden.
focus: Adapt the interview to sensory discomfort
topicTitle: A headache is not a whole history

title: The zigzag happened before the sentence
setting: Romy describes seeing zigzag lines and struggling to find a word during a previous headache episode.
hook: Romy describes seeing zigzag lines and struggling to find a word during a previous headache episode. She is now at a follow-up, but the timing in the original note is unclear. Her drawing is remarkably precise about the zigzags and entirely vague about the clock. You need to establish what happened first, how long it lasted, whether it was new and whether anything is happening now. Do not casually label every visual or speech symptom as aura, especially if a new acute problem emerges during the discussion.
question: Romy describes visual and speech symptoms from a prior event. What should you establish before interpreting them?
options: Label all visual and speech changes as harmless aura
Assign exact durations because the drawing is detailed
Clarify current status and the past sequence without guessing
feedback: The correct move separates an active concern from a historical reconstruction. New acute neurological symptoms must not be casually filed under aura. A detailed drawing does not establish timing. Ask what Romy actually remembers, document gaps and ensure the clinician interprets the complete account rather than a polished invented sequence.
handover: Frau Keller schildert rückblickend visuelle Phänomene und mögliche Wortfindungsprobleme bei einem Ereignis der Vorwoche. Reihenfolge und Dauer sind teilweise unklar; aktuelle Beschwerden wurden zeitlich davon abgegrenzt, eine diagnostische Einordnung steht aus.
focus: Clarify sequence and novelty of neurological symptoms
topicTitle: A headache is not a whole history

title: The packet count is not the day count
setting: Felix says he takes pain medicine occasionally.
hook: Felix says he takes pain medicine occasionally. His calendar shows frequent headaches, but he counts packets rather than days and uses different products depending on which shop is open. A cupboard labelled important things contains both receipts and several half-empty boxes. He is attending a planned headache review, with no acute warning symptoms supplied in the case. You need to clarify actual use and symptom frequency, avoiding blame and avoiding a new medication plan based on the vague word occasionally.
question: Felix counts packets rather than medicine-use days. What should the headache review clarify?
options: Clarify days and products for clinical review
Accept occasionally as a complete medication history
Declare medication-overuse headache without assessing the pattern
feedback: The useful move turns a vague frequency into a more reliable account. The initial word does not answer how often different medicines are used. A diagnosis about overuse would require proper assessment. Gather the pattern neutrally, identify uncertain details and let the clinician use it to review the individual plan.
handover: Herr Braun beschreibt seine Analgetikaeinnahme zunächst als gelegentlich, nennt jedoch Packungsmengen statt Einnahmetagen. Kopfschmerz- und Einnahmehäufigkeit sowie Präparate werden konkretisiert; eine medikamentenbedingte Ursache ist damit noch nicht gesichert.
focus: Ask about headache medicine use by days and products
topicTitle: A headache is not a whole history

title: Her father’s scan is not her scan
setting: Luisa’s father had a brain tumour, and her recent headaches have brought back the waiting-room memories more vividly than she expected.
hook: Luisa’s father had a brain tumour, and her recent headaches have brought back the waiting-room memories more vividly than she expected. She asks for reassurance but really means certainty. Her partner has tried to help by saying everyone gets headaches, which has made her feel less able to explain why these worry her. No diagnosis or scan result is provided. You need to acknowledge the family experience, assess the actual headache pattern and explain what can and cannot be concluded today.
question: Luisa fears her headache means the same tumour her father had. How should you respond?
options: Promise no tumour because headaches are common
Acknowledge the fear and assess her own symptom pattern
Assume her father’s illness proves the same diagnosis
feedback: The correct response addresses both the emotional context and the clinical question. Neither commonness nor family experience proves the cause. Clarify the present headache, escalate any concerning features and explain the plan. Avoid using a reassuring tone to disguise a claim that cannot be supported by the available evidence.
handover: Frau Arnold berichtet über Kopfschmerzen und ausgeprägte Sorge wegen eines Hirntumors beim Vater. Ihre eigene Symptomatik ist gezielt zu beurteilen; eine intrakranielle Ursache ist durch das Gespräch allein weder nachgewiesen noch ausgeschlossen.
focus: Respond to fear of a brain tumour
topicTitle: A headache is not a whole history

title: The diary does not need a design award
setting: Milo was advised to record headaches and arrived with a spreadsheet containing seventeen colours, six tabs and no entries after Tuesday.
hook: Milo was advised to record headaches and arrived with a spreadsheet containing seventeen colours, six tabs and no entries after Tuesday. He spent longer designing it than observing the symptoms. He is attending a review of recurrent headaches and wants to know what information would actually help. The communication task is to agree a simple, achievable way of noting episodes and relevant context with the treating team, rather than turning the diary into another demanding task or assuming every coinciding event is a proven trigger.
question: Milo’s elaborate headache diary is mostly empty. What would make it more useful?
options: Require every cell before offering further discussion
Treat every coinciding food as a confirmed trigger
Agree a small usable record and review it together
feedback: The useful move makes the task achievable and keeps interpretation cautious. An incomplete diary is not a reason to withhold attention. Coincidence does not establish a trigger. Choose relevant observations, discuss gaps openly and use the record alongside clinical assessment rather than as a substitute for it.
handover: Herr Schenk konnte ein sehr umfangreiches Kopfschmerztagebuch nicht regelmäßig führen. Ein alltagstauglicher Umfang wird mit ihm und dem Behandlungsteam abgestimmt; aus möglichen zeitlichen Zusammenhängen werden keine gesicherten Auslöser abgeleitet.
focus: Create a manageable symptom diary conversation
topicTitle: A headache is not a whole history

title: The scan request meets the small-space worry
setting: Dora has been offered an imaging discussion after assessment of headaches.
hook: Dora has been offered an imaging discussion after assessment of headaches. She says yes quickly because she wants an answer, then asks whether the scanner is a closed space. Her previous experience in a stuck lift has made enclosed spaces difficult. The referral does not tell you which accommodations are possible or even confirm the final imaging plan. You need to bring the concern into the planning conversation, not promise that every scan is effortless or let a quick yes conceal a significant fear.
question: Dora agreed quickly to imaging but fears enclosed spaces. What needs clarification before the plan proceeds?
options: Clarify the actual scan and discuss support with its team
Promise there will be no discomfort or anxiety
Cancel all assessment without exploring the concern
feedback: The correct move makes the fear part of an individual plan. A blanket comfort promise may be false, while abandoning assessment immediately may be unnecessary. Verify the investigation, explain its process with the responsible team and discuss available support so Dora can make an informed decision rather than simply endure or withdraw.
handover: Frau Klein äußert Angst vor engen Räumen im Zusammenhang mit einer möglichen bildgebenden Untersuchung. Untersuchungsart, Ablauf und verfügbare Unterstützung werden mit dem zuständigen Team geklärt; eine endgültige Einwilligung wird nicht aus der ersten Zustimmung abgeleitet.
focus: Elicit an imaging concern before consent
topicTitle: A headache is not a whole history

title: Migraine is not another word for a bad mood
setting: Samira’s colleagues call her headaches a bad mood with better branding.
hook: Samira’s colleagues call her headaches a bad mood with better branding. She laughs along, then admits that episodes can interrupt reading and make ordinary light uncomfortable. She wants language for explaining the impact at work without sharing every personal detail. The case does not establish the current diagnosis or authorise disclosure to her employer. You need to understand the functional burden, support a respectful explanation and coordinate any formal documentation with the responsible clinician while checking the actual symptom pattern.
question: Samira wants to explain functional limits at work without sharing everything. What should you agree?
options: Tell the employer her full medical history without asking
Describe functional needs and agree the disclosure scope
Dismiss the impact because she can joke about it
feedback: The useful move recognises the burden and preserves control over disclosure. Humour does not prove symptoms are minor. A workplace request does not authorise unrestricted information sharing. Clarify the actual clinical situation, agree useful wording and coordinate formal documentation without inventing findings or guaranteeing how others will respond.
handover: Frau Roth berichtet über durch Kopfschmerzepisoden beeinträchtigtes Lesen und Lichtempfindlichkeit und wünscht eine begrenzte arbeitsbezogene Erklärung. Klinische Einordnung und gewünschter Informationsumfang werden getrennt geklärt; eine Arbeitgebermitteilung ist noch nicht freigegeben.
focus: Validate impact and agree a functional explanation
topicTitle: A headache is not a whole history

title: The missing minute belongs to the witness
setting: Tom is being interviewed after an acute assessment of an episode his partner witnessed at breakfast.
hook: Tom is being interviewed after an acute assessment of an episode his partner witnessed at breakfast. He remembers reaching for a cup and then hearing several people say his name. His partner describes stiffening and jerking, but Tom cannot confirm the middle of the event because he does not remember it. The breakfast toast has become the least important unfinished task in the house. Your job is to record both accounts accurately, not persuade Tom to describe movements he did not experience consciously or merge the witness’s estimate with a measured duration.
question: Tom cannot remember the movements his partner saw. How should you combine their accounts?
options: Attribute patient memory and witness observations separately
Record no jerking because he cannot remember it
Convert the witness’s rough estimate into an exact timed duration
feedback: The correct move preserves the source of each fact. Lack of memory is not evidence that an observed event did not occur. A rough estimate should not become a precise measurement. Ask about the sequence, distinguish observation from interpretation and provide the team with a traceable account rather than a falsely seamless narrative.
handover: Herr Berger erinnert sich an die Zeit vor und nach einer Erinnerungslücke; die Partnerin berichtet über Versteifung und Zuckungen. Eigen- und Fremdanamnese sowie geschätzte Dauer werden getrennt dokumentiert; die diagnostische Einordnung ist noch offen.
focus: Separate recalled experience from witnessed seizure features

title: One event, a lifetime of questions
setting: Clara is attending specialist follow-up after a first suspected seizure.
hook: Clara is attending specialist follow-up after a first suspected seizure. She has already changed her social-media profile to say she has epilepsy because that was the word she recognised in the referral. She is frightened about what this means for the rest of her life. The available information does not establish the diagnosis. You need to explain that an event and a condition are not interchangeable labels, while taking the event seriously and preserving the need for assessment rather than promising that it will never happen again.
question: Clara assumes a first suspected seizure confirms lifelong epilepsy. What should you explain?
options: Confirm lifelong epilepsy from the referral word
Explain event versus diagnosis and the need for follow-up
Guarantee that a first event cannot recur
feedback: The useful response avoids both premature labelling and dismissal. A referral term does not establish a lifelong condition, and a first event does not justify a guarantee against recurrence. Clarify the evidence, support specialist follow-up and give Clara space to discuss practical concerns without answering them through speculation.
handover: Frau Sommer stellt sich nach einem ersten vermuteten Anfallsereignis zur Nachbesprechung vor. Eine Epilepsiediagnose ist nach den hier verfügbaren Angaben nicht gesichert; Ursache und individuelle Konsequenzen sind fachärztlich zu klären.
focus: Distinguish a seizure event from an epilepsy diagnosis

title: The second event changes the priority
setting: Robert has another episode of jerking before recovering normally from the first.
hook: Robert has another episode of jerking before recovering normally from the first. The team member taking background details has not yet reached the allergy section. His companion asks whether this can wait until the history is finished because he has had episodes before. No individual rescue plan is available in the scene. The communication task is to stop the routine interview and summon emergency clinical help immediately, making the lack of recovery between events explicit rather than treating a previous history as reassurance.
question: Robert has another event before recovering from the first. What takes priority?
options: Complete background questions before escalating
Assume previous episodes mean this one is safe
Call emergency help now and state the absent recovery
feedback: The correct move responds to repeated events without recovery as an emergency concern. Routine completion delays help, and prior episodes do not establish present safety. Communicate the sequence and current condition, bring available records to the responding team and leave individual emergency treatment to the clinicians assessing Robert.
handover: Bei Herrn Lenz wird ein erneutes Ereignis mit Zuckungen beobachtet, ohne dass er sich zwischenzeitlich regelrecht erholt hat. Das Notfallteam wird sofort alarmiert; ein individueller Notfallplan liegt aktuell nicht vor und wird ohne Verzögerung der Hilfe gesucht.
focus: Escalate repeated seizures without recovery

title: The normal page is not the whole film
setting: Isabel’s routine EEG report is described as normal, and she wants to cancel the specialist follow-up.
hook: Isabel’s routine EEG report is described as normal, and she wants to cancel the specialist follow-up. She imagines the test would have captured every possible problem, like a security camera recording all night. Her original event still needs interpretation, and the full clinical assessment is not supplied in this scene. You need to explain that a recording samples activity during a period and must be interpreted with the history, without making the normal result sound either meaningless or a universal exclusion of seizures.
question: Isabel thinks a normal EEG makes follow-up unnecessary. What should you explain?
options: Explain the limits and keep the interpretation appointment
Cancel follow-up because a normal EEG excludes epilepsy
Say the EEG result has no value at all
feedback: The useful response gives the result an appropriate place in the assessment. A normal recording alone does not rule out epilepsy. Calling it worthless would be another overstatement. Review the event account and findings with the specialist, making clear that the result’s meaning depends on the wider clinical picture.
handover: Frau König berichtet über einen unauffällig befundeten Routine-EEG-Befund und möchte die weitere Besprechung absagen. Ein Anfallsleiden ist dadurch allein nicht ausgeschlossen; die Einordnung mit Ereignisanamnese und weiteren Befunden bleibt erforderlich.
focus: Explain the limits of a normal EEG

title: The van keys on the desk
setting: Murat makes deliveries for a small business and puts his van keys on the desk during follow-up after a suspected seizure.
hook: Murat makes deliveries for a small business and puts his van keys on the desk during follow-up after a suspected seizure. He asks when he can drive again because the business cannot run on apologies. The individual diagnosis, licensing category and applicable assessment have not been established in this scene. Your task is to take the livelihood concern seriously, avoid giving clearance, and arrange specific advice from the responsible specialist about safety and the applicable rules rather than borrowing a generic time limit from another country or case.
question: Murat wants a driving return date after a suspected seizure. What can you responsibly offer?
options: Give a universal return-to-driving date from memory
Arrange specific advice and practical alternatives without clearance
Say he may drive if he personally feels fine
feedback: The correct move respects the livelihood issue and the limits of available information. Feeling fine does not establish fitness to drive, and a universal date may be wrong. Obtain individual specialist advice and the applicable requirements, then help Murat identify practical support without making an unverified legal or clinical promise.
handover: Herr Fischer benötigt nach einem vermuteten Anfallsereignis eine individuelle Beratung zur Fahreignung und beruflichen Situation. Eine Freigabe oder feste Frist wird hier nicht erteilt; zuständige fachärztliche Beurteilung und geltende Vorgaben werden geklärt.
focus: Address driving concerns without inventing legal clearance

title: The party question without a raised eyebrow
setting: Lotte is attending a review after an episode that occurred the morning after a celebration.
