hook: Lotte is attending a review after an episode that occurred the morning after a celebration. She mentions little sleep but hesitates about alcohol because she expects a raised eyebrow and a lecture. The party playlist is still being debated in the family chat; the event itself needs a more useful account. You need to ask neutral, specific questions about sleep, substances, illness and medicines, without declaring that one disclosed exposure proves the cause or turning a sensitive question into a moral judgment.
question: Lotte fears blame when discussing sleep and alcohol before an event. How should you ask?
options: Tell her the celebration definitely caused the event
Avoid substance questions entirely to spare embarrassment
Ask neutrally and separate possible contributors from cause
feedback: The useful move gathers relevant information without judgment. Declaring a cause from the party alone is premature, while avoiding the topic leaves an important gap. Ask specifically and respectfully, record uncertainty and pass the account for clinical interpretation together with the rest of the event history.
handover: Frau Neumann berichtet über Schlafmangel und Alkoholkonsum vor dem Ereignis. Menge, Zeitpunkt und weitere mögliche Einflussfaktoren werden neutral erfragt; ein ursächlicher Zusammenhang wird dadurch nicht als gesichert dargestellt.
focus: Ask about possible precipitants without assigning blame

title: The question saved for next year
setting: Sophie has established epilepsy and is attending a planned review.
hook: Sophie has established epilepsy and is attending a planned review. At the end she mentions that she and her partner may want a baby next year. She has read alarming medicine information online and wonders whether stopping her treatment now would be the responsible thing to do. Her current regimen and individual risks are not supplied. You need to recognise the importance of the question, arrange specialist review and clearly avoid an unsupervised change, without promising a risk-free pregnancy or choosing a replacement drug in this communication exercise.
question: Sophie considers stopping epilepsy medicine while planning pregnancy. What should you communicate?
options: Arrange specialist planning and advise against independent changes
Tell her to stop treatment immediately
Promise all epilepsy medicines are harmless in pregnancy
feedback: The correct move turns an important future question into a supported individual review. Abrupt self-directed changes can be unsafe, and blanket claims about pregnancy safety are inaccurate. Confirm the existing plan, arrange specialist counselling and explain what Sophie should clarify without making a medication decision from missing information.
handover: Frau Lang mit berichteter bekannter Epilepsie plant eine Schwangerschaft und erwägt eigenständiges Absetzen ihrer Medikation. Eine zeitnahe fachärztliche Beratung wird organisiert; Präparat und individueller Plan werden verifiziert, eigenständige Änderungen werden nicht empfohlen.
focus: Invite pregnancy planning discussion without abrupt medicine changes

title: A recording is evidence, not entertainment
setting: Daniela’s colleague recorded part of an episode and offers to show it during follow-up.
hook: Daniela’s colleague recorded part of an episode and offers to show it during follow-up. Daniela is grateful that someone may have captured useful information, but she does not want the video forwarded through the workplace chat. The colleague has already called it “the evidence,” which makes her feel as though she is on trial. The communication task is to clarify her wishes, arrange appropriate clinical review through approved channels and keep the recording’s limits visible: it shows only what the camera captured during that interval.
question: Daniela wants clinical use of a witness video without workplace circulation. How should you proceed?
options: Forward the video to colleagues through a personal chat
Agree appropriate clinical review and document the clip’s limits
Treat the short clip as a complete diagnostic record
feedback: The useful move protects dignity while preserving possible clinical value. Unrestricted forwarding is not necessary for assessment, and a partial recording cannot supply missing context. Clarify Daniela’s wishes, follow the approved process and combine the clip with attributed history rather than letting the camera replace the conversation.
handover: Frau Kraus möchte die Weitergabe eines durch einen Kollegen aufgenommenen Teilvideos begrenzen. Eine mögliche klinische Sichtung wird mit ihr über geeignete Wege abgestimmt; der Anfallsbeginn ist nicht enthalten und die Aufnahme ersetzt keine vollständige Ereignisanamnese.
focus: Handle a witness video with consent and dignity

title: The presentation has lost its presenter
setting: Clara arrives at the practice carrying a laptop and a scarf.
hook: Clara arrives at the practice carrying a laptop and a scarf. Her throat has hurt since yesterday, and tomorrow she is supposed to present a proposal to twenty people. She asks for something that will guarantee her voice works by nine. Her slides are ready; apparently her tonsils have not accepted the calendar invitation. You have not examined her yet. Behind the request for an instant cure is a practical worry: she cannot afford to promise her manager something she cannot deliver.
question: How can you respond to Clara’s presentation deadline without promising recovery?
options: Promise that rest will restore her voice overnight.
Explore her symptoms and explain that tomorrow’s fitness is uncertain.
Discuss slide design before asking about swallowing.
feedback: The second choice addresses both the symptoms and the real deadline. A recovery promise cannot be justified before assessment; changing the subject misses her concern.
handover: Frau Seidel berichtet seit gestern über Halsschmerzen sowie Beschwerden beim Schlucken und längeren Sprechen. Sie wünscht eine Einschätzung zur Arbeitsfähigkeit morgen; Untersuchung und weitere Anamnese stehen noch aus.
focus: Explore the real goal without promising recovery

title: The thermometer is still in the drawer
setting: Jonas tells reception that he has a high fever and a sore throat.
hook: Jonas tells reception that he has a high fever and a sore throat. In the room, he explains that he felt hot while unloading shopping, but never used the thermometer at home. His partner bought a clever digital one; nobody has yet won the argument about its buttons. The referral box already says fever confirmed. You need to preserve Jonas’s experience while correcting the difference between feeling feverish and a measured temperature. Neither dismissing him nor inventing a number will help.
question: How should Jonas’s unmeasured fever be recorded?
options: Clarify whether the temperature was measured.
Choose a plausible temperature for the record.
Tell Jonas that feeling hot does not count.
feedback: Clarifying the source preserves useful information. Guessing creates false evidence, while dismissing the feeling discourages Jonas from describing a real change in how he feels.
handover: Herr Feld berichtet über Halsschmerzen und ein Fiebergefühl. Eine Temperaturmessung zu Hause erfolgte nach seiner Aussage nicht; ein Messwert liegt im Gespräch nicht vor.
focus: Distinguish a reported symptom from a measurement

title: A medicine box with a long memory
setting: Mina brings a partly used antibiotic box from an old cupboard.
hook: Mina brings a partly used antibiotic box from an old cupboard. Her throat hurts and she wants to know whether the remaining tablets will save a return visit. The cupboard is her family’s unofficial archive: spare batteries, birthday candles and medicines all live there without a filing system. She has not taken the tablets this time. You need to respond without praising self-treatment or shaming her for asking. The useful opening is that she brought the package instead of guessing its name.
question: What should happen before discussing Mina’s leftover antibiotic?
options: Recommend whatever tablets remain.
Lecture her about keeping cupboards tidy.
Assess the present illness before discussing appropriate treatment.
feedback: Assessment addresses the actual question safely. An old prescription does not decide today’s treatment; a lecture about storage would distract from symptoms and discourage future disclosure.
handover: Frau Berger berichtet über aktuelle Halsschmerzen und fragt nach der Einnahme übrig gebliebener Antibiotika. Sie gibt an, diese bisher nicht eingenommen zu haben; die Ursache der Beschwerden ist noch ungeklärt.
focus: Handle a request for leftover antibiotics without judgement

title: Breathing changes the throat interview
setting: Emir is being asked about a sore throat when he reports that breathing has become difficult.
hook: Emir is being asked about a sore throat when he reports that breathing has become difficult. His voice sounds strained, and he is frightened. The history form still has several empty sections, including travel and family history. This is no longer an exercise in completing every box in the correct order. Your task is to recognise that the conversation has changed, stop routine questioning and summon the clinical team immediately. Stay with short, clear language while help is being organised.
question: What takes priority when Emir reports new breathing difficulty?
options: Finish the checklist first.
Stop questioning and summon the clinical team immediately.
Explain every possible throat diagnosis.
feedback: The second choice responds to a new potentially serious symptom. Completing routine history or giving a long explanation delays the clinical assessment that Emir now needs.
handover: Herr Lorenz berichtet während der Anamnese über neu aufgetretene Atemnot bei Halsschmerzen; die Stimme wirkt angestrengt. Die Routineanamnese wurde unterbrochen und das Behandlungsteam sofort angefordert; Vitalparameter sind hier nicht dokumentiert.
focus: Interrupt a routine history for urgent assessment

title: The group chat is not a laboratory
setting: Nora arrives worried that she has infectious mononucleosis because two people in her university group chat mentioned it.
hook: Nora arrives worried that she has infectious mononucleosis because two people in her university group chat mentioned it. She has a sore throat and feels unusually tired. The chat has already produced a diagnosis, three home remedies and a proposed cancellation of next month’s picnic. Nobody has examined her. She wants you to say which message is right. You need to acknowledge why the story sounds plausible while explaining what is still unknown and which questions come before conclusions.
question: How can you respond to Nora’s group-chat diagnosis?
options: Agree with the group chat.
Say that online conversations are always worthless.
Explain what is possible and what information is still needed.
feedback: The third choice offers a path through uncertainty. Agreement invents certainty, while dismissing the group chat dismisses the reason Nora is concerned without answering her question.
handover: Frau Winter berichtet über Halsschmerzen und ungewöhnliche Müdigkeit sowie ähnliche Erkrankungen im Bekanntenkreis. Eine infektiöse Mononukleose ist eine mögliche Erklärung; Untersuchung und diagnostische Einordnung stehen aus.
focus: Explain diagnostic uncertainty without sounding evasive

title: A question without an audience
setting: Leonie comes with her father, who answers quickly whenever you ask about her recent illness.
hook: Leonie comes with her father, who answers quickly whenever you ask about her recent illness. She looks at him before every reply. When you ask about close contacts, he begins listing everyone who attended a family dinner. Leonie quietly says she would rather talk alone for part of the appointment. There is no need to turn this into a family confrontation. The skill is to make private conversation feel ordinary, respect an adult patient’s preference and avoid announcing sensitive assumptions to the room.
question: How should you respond to Leonie’s request to speak alone?
options: Offer a private conversation and clarify sharing preferences.
Ask the father to approve her request.
Announce possible sensitive diagnoses before he leaves.
feedback: The first choice follows the adult patient’s request. Seeking permission from the companion reverses that relationship; speculating aloud could disclose information Leonie has not chosen to share.
handover: Frau Graf wünscht für einen Teil der Anamnese ein Gespräch ohne ihren Vater. Ihre Freigabe zur Weitergabe von Informationen wird gesondert geklärt; Angaben zu Kontakten sind noch nicht vollständig erhoben.
focus: Arrange private adult history-taking naturally

title: The allergy has a missing chapter
setting: Paul’s record contains the word penicillin with three exclamation marks.
hook: Paul’s record contains the word penicillin with three exclamation marks. When you ask, he remembers red spots after a medicine years ago but is unsure which medicine it was. The family version of the story has become more dramatic each Christmas. He is here with a sore throat and worries that no treatment will be possible. Your job is neither to erase the warning nor promote a vague memory into a confirmed severe reaction. Recover the details that can actually be known.
question: What can you safely record about Paul’s uncertain reaction?
options: Delete the warning because the story is old.
Document the remembered reaction and explicitly mark the gaps.
Write anaphylaxis because the record uses exclamation marks.
feedback: The second choice preserves information without inventing severity. Age does not invalidate a reaction; punctuation cannot establish what happened or which medicine caused it.
handover: Herr Henning erinnert einen Hautausschlag nach einer früheren Medikamenteneinnahme; Präparat, zeitlicher Abstand und weitere Symptome sind unklar. Eine Penicillinallergie ist in der Akte vermerkt, aber im Gespräch nicht näher bestätigt.
focus: Clarify a reported medication reaction

title: The cough arrives halfway through
setting: Svenja booked the visit for a sore throat.
hook: Svenja booked the visit for a sore throat. Halfway through the conversation she mentions a cough and discomfort when taking a deep breath, then apologises for adding things late. She had assumed the booking reason was the only symptom she was allowed to discuss. Her handbag contains a carefully numbered list, which suddenly feels less useful than the detail she nearly omitted. You need to reopen the story rather than defend the original appointment label or decide the cause before assessing her.
question: What changes when Svenja mentions cough and pain on breathing?
options: Keep to the original booking label.
Diagnose pneumonia from the new sentence alone.
Reassess the story and include the new symptoms.
feedback: The third choice uses the new information without jumping to a conclusion. Ignoring it narrows assessment unfairly; a symptom combination alone does not confirm a diagnosis.
handover: Frau Roth berichtet neben Halsschmerzen über Husten und Schmerzen beim tiefen Einatmen. Die Dauer und weitere Begleitsymptome werden noch geklärt; eine diagnostische Zuordnung ist bislang nicht erfolgt.
focus: Reopen the symptom story when new information appears

title: The wrist changed sides on paper
setting: Tobias slipped beside his bicycle and landed on his right hand.
hook: Tobias slipped beside his bicycle and landed on his right hand. The referral says left wrist, while he keeps protecting the right one. He jokes that the form must have used a mirror. He also mentions a sore area on his chest from the handlebar. You are about to summarise the history for a colleague. This is the moment to check the mismatch with Tobias, not choose whichever side appears in the more official-looking document or quietly forget the second injury.
question: Which side and which injuries belong in Tobias’s handover?
options: Trust the printed side.
Confirm the side and include both injury sites.
Mention only the wrist because it hurts more.
feedback: The second option repairs the discrepancy and preserves the associated complaint. Neither a printed form nor pain ranking justifies discarding what Tobias reports.
handover: Herr Kern berichtet einen Sturz auf die rechte Hand sowie Schmerzen am Thorax nach Lenkerkontakt. Die Überweisung nennt abweichend links; Untersuchungsbefunde liegen hier noch nicht vor.
focus: Resolve conflicting laterality before handover
topicTitle: The day did not go to plan

title: A delivery route waiting outside
setting: Amira has wrist pain after falling on a pavement.
hook: Amira has wrist pain after falling on a pavement. She keeps looking at her van keys because six deliveries remain and her supervisor wants an arrival time. She can move some fingers and takes that as proof that nothing can be broken. The route app continues to announce that she is late, demonstrating excellent timing and very little empathy. You need to acknowledge her work pressure while explaining why movement alone cannot settle the injury question or justify a return-to-driving promise.
question: What can finger movement tell you about Amira’s readiness to drive?
options: Recommend finishing the route first.
Ignore the work question entirely.
Explain the uncertainty and assess before discussing work.
feedback: The third option addresses both injury and work. Returning to deliveries assumes safety; ignoring the route leaves the pressure that may drive Amira to leave unaddressed.
handover: Frau König berichtet Handgelenkschmerzen nach einem Sturz und erhaltene Fingerbeweglichkeit. Sie fragt nach Fortsetzung ihrer Lieferfahrt; eine Fraktur ist durch diese Angabe nicht ausgeschlossen und die Untersuchung steht aus.
focus: Correct a reassuring assumption without dismissing practical stakes
topicTitle: The day did not go to plan

title: The hip that almost stayed off the list
setting: Ralf comes in after tripping over a doorstep, holding his wrist as if it were a fragile parcel.
hook: Ralf comes in after tripping over a doorstep, holding his wrist as if it were a fragile parcel. When asked about other pain, he mentions his hip but says it does not deserve attention because the wrist is worse. He lives above a shop with a staircase and had planned to carry groceries upstairs. You have not assessed either injury yet. The conversation needs to include function and other painful areas without asking him to demonstrate walking simply to prove that he can.
question: How should Ralf’s less painful hip complaint be handled?
options: Ask about the hip and include it in assessment.
Document only the wrist.
Ask him to climb stairs now.
feedback: The first choice keeps both injuries visible. The alternatives either erase a relevant symptom or ask for a demonstration before the injury has been assessed.
handover: Herr Sommer berichtet nach einem Stolpersturz über Handgelenkschmerzen und bewegungsabhängige Leistenschmerzen. Eine Gehprobe wurde im Gespräch nicht veranlasst; die Verletzungen sind noch nicht untersucht.
focus: Find associated injury without unsafe demonstration
topicTitle: The day did not go to plan

title: A new feeling under the support
setting: Elena is waiting after a wrist injury when she reports new tingling in her fingers.
hook: Elena is waiting after a wrist injury when she reports new tingling in her fingers. Earlier she had mainly described pain, so the waiting note still says unchanged. She worries about bothering staff again and introduces the update with an apology. This is not the time for a joke or a reassuring guess about tight clothing. You need to make the new symptom visible, arrange prompt clinical reassessment and keep the original timeline rather than retrospectively writing that the tingling was always present.
question: What should you do with Elena’s newly reported tingling?
options: Copy unchanged from the old note.
Escalate the new symptom and record its onset.
Explain that everyone has tingling when anxious.
feedback: The second option treats the change as useful information. Copying the old note hides it; attributing it to anxiety without assessment creates an unsupported explanation.
handover: Frau Rauch berichtet nach Handgelenkverletzung über seit wenigen Minuten neu aufgetretenes Fingerkribbeln. Eine zeitnahe erneute klinische Beurteilung wurde angefordert; Durchblutung, Motorik und Sensibilität sind hier nicht untersucht.
focus: Escalate a change while preserving timing
topicTitle: The day did not go to plan

title: A blurry photograph of an important tablet
setting: Boris has fallen onto his wrist and hip.
hook: Boris has fallen onto his wrist and hip. He says he takes something to thin the blood but cannot recall the name. His daughter sends a photograph of a medicine box; the glare covers the exact word you need. Boris offers a confident guess based on the colour of the tablet. You need to communicate that the medication detail matters, seek reliable confirmation and mark it unknown meanwhile. The photograph is a clue, not permission to select a familiar drug from memory.
question: How should Boris’s unidentified blood thinner be handled?
options: Choose the most common blood thinner.
Leave medicines out until tomorrow.
Seek verification and hand over the uncertainty now.
feedback: The third option makes progress without false precision. Guessing risks a wrong record, while postponing the whole topic hides a potentially important part of the injury history.
handover: Herr Engel berichtet nach Sturz auf Hand und Hüfte die Einnahme eines blutverdünnenden Medikaments. Präparat und letzte Einnahme sind noch unbestätigt; eine Klärung anhand des Plans beziehungsweise der Packung wird angestrebt.
focus: Reconcile important medicines without guessing
topicTitle: The day did not go to plan

title: The neighbour knows the pavement, not the pain
setting: Hannah’s neighbour saw her trip and kindly brought her to the clinic.
hook: Hannah’s neighbour saw her trip and kindly brought her to the clinic. He describes the pavement, the weather and the exact position of a recycling bin with the precision of a town planner. Hannah keeps trying to explain what hurt first. The witness account may be useful, but it should not replace her account of symptoms. You need to invite Hannah’s story, then ask the neighbour what he actually saw, keeping observation and interpretation separate without making him feel unwelcome.
question: Whose account should describe Hannah’s pain and the fall?
options: Hear Hannah first and attribute the two accounts.
Accept the neighbour’s full interpretation.
Ask the neighbour to leave without hearing relevant observations.
feedback: The first choice preserves both perspectives. Replacing Hannah’s story silences symptoms; rejecting the witness entirely loses potentially useful facts about the event.
handover: Frau Voigt berichtet nach einem Stolpersturz zunächst Hüftschmerzen. Der Nachbar war Zeuge; seine Beobachtungen zum Hergang werden getrennt von den Beschwerden der Patientin erhoben.
focus: Separate witness observation from patient experience
topicTitle: The day did not go to plan

title: The violin lesson needs a different answer
setting: Martin teaches violin and has injured his wrist while moving a bookcase.
hook: Martin teaches violin and has injured his wrist while moving a bookcase. He asks whether he will play normally next Tuesday, then opens a calendar packed with students. The bookcase survived with more dignity than the appointment schedule. You do not yet have examination or imaging results. He is not asking for a lecture on every fracture type; he needs to know what can be said now and when a more useful answer about function might become possible.
question: What can you honestly tell Martin about next Tuesday’s lesson?
options: Give a standard recovery date.
Explain the missing assessment and plan the next discussion.
Avoid answering because he is a musician.
feedback: The second choice is honest and practical. A generic date ignores the unknown injury; silence leaves Martin without any way to manage the immediate scheduling problem.
handover: Herr Falk fragt nach Wiederaufnahme des Geigenspiels nach Handgelenkverletzung. Klinische und bildgebende Befunde liegen hier noch nicht vor; eine belastbare Prognose zur Funktion wurde daher nicht gegeben.
focus: Discuss prognosis as staged information
topicTitle: The day did not go to plan

title: Normal is not a default setting
setting: Selin is being handed over after a fall onto her wrist.
hook: Selin is being handed over after a fall onto her wrist. The note template offers a convenient button labelled circulation, movement and sensation normal. You have asked about pain but have not performed that examination. The button would make the page look reassuringly complete, which is exactly the problem. Your colleague needs an honest account of what remains to be checked, not a record that looks tidier than the work behind it. Selin is still waiting for the clinical assessment.
question: What should replace the unexamined normal finding in Selin’s record?
options: Keep the default normal entry.
Erase the whole injury history.
Correct the finding to not yet assessed.
feedback: The third choice repairs the specific false statement. Keeping the default invents evidence; deleting the whole history would remove valid patient information along with the error.
handover: Frau Adler wird nach Sturz auf das Handgelenk vorgestellt. Die periphere Durchblutung, Motorik und Sensibilität wurden im vorliegenden Gespräch nicht untersucht; ein voreingestellter Normalbefund wurde korrigiert.
focus: Document an unperformed examination honestly
topicTitle: The day did not go to plan

title: The dashboard was closer than expected
setting: Daria’s knee struck the dashboard when the car stopped suddenly.
hook: Daria’s knee struck the dashboard when the car stopped suddenly. Her friend drove, but the first note calls her the driver. She is anxious that correcting the detail will sound like blaming someone. Her knee hurts and she also mentions hip pain. You are collecting the injury story, not deciding responsibility for the road incident. Calm, neutral questions can separate seating position, impact and symptoms without turning the consultation into an interrogation or leaving an inaccurate mechanism in the record.
question: How can you correct Daria’s seating position without assigning blame?
options: Ask who deserves blame.
Clarify seating and impact neutrally.
Keep the driver label to avoid discomfort.
feedback: The second option obtains the relevant mechanism and corrects the record. Blame is not the clinical task; avoiding a correction leaves a factual error in place.
handover: Frau Blum berichtet als Beifahrerin über einen Anprall des Knies am Armaturenbrett und zusätzliche Hüftschmerzen. Die bisherige Angabe als Fahrerin wurde berichtigt; Untersuchungsbefunde stehen aus.
focus: Ask mechanism questions without assigning blame

title: The wedding is booked; the ankle is not
setting: Benno twisted his ankle stepping off a curb and is due to dance at his sister’s wedding on Saturday.
hook: Benno twisted his ankle stepping off a curb and is due to dance at his sister’s wedding on Saturday. He asks whether a brace will make him ready. The carefully polished shoes in his bag suggest that the reception has already passed its wardrobe inspection. You have not established the injury. He needs an honest conversation about the event without a promise that a support device cancels pain or makes every activity safe. Start with what he can describe, not the dance timetable.
question: What should come before advice about Benno’s wedding dance?
options: Assess first, then discuss realistic participation.
Recommend a brace as a guarantee.
Tell him the wedding does not matter.
feedback: The first choice joins assessment to the patient’s goal. A device guarantee bypasses uncertainty; dismissing the event ignores why Benno is asking now.
handover: Herr Hart berichtet ein Umknickereignis am Bordstein und fragt nach Tanzfähigkeit am Wochenende. Eine genaue Verletzungsdiagnose und individuelle Belastungsempfehlung liegen noch nicht vor.
focus: Handle an activity deadline without promising device-based safety

title: Home has forty-two steps
setting: Hella’s knee hurts after a fall, and she lives on the third floor without a lift.
hook: Hella’s knee hurts after a fall, and she lives on the third floor without a lift. She is less worried about the medical name than about reaching her flat and feeding her cat. Her neighbour has the spare key but not the cat’s approval. The examination is still pending. You need to ask about practical support and the home layout without promising discharge or asking her to prove that she can manage stairs. Planning starts with the real environment she will return to.
question: How should Hella’s stairs influence this conversation?
options: Assume someone will help.
Ask her to climb stairs immediately.
Clarify the home situation and include it in planning.
feedback: The third option gathers information needed for a realistic plan. Assuming support invents a resource; a stair demonstration before assessment may be inappropriate.
handover: Frau Neumann berichtet Knieschmerzen nach Sturz und eine Wohnung im dritten Stock ohne Aufzug. Unterstützung und Versorgung zu Hause müssen in die weitere Planung einbezogen werden; die Verletzungsbeurteilung steht aus.
focus: Include home circumstances in a functional conversation

title: The support has a material question
setting: Oskar mentions a previous skin reaction to latex as someone discusses an ankle support.
hook: Oskar mentions a previous skin reaction to latex as someone discusses an ankle support. He cannot say which brand caused it, but remembers itchy redness where a product touched his skin. He is embarrassed because he thinks a material question sounds fussy compared with an injury. His hiking spreadsheet includes weather, snacks and emergency socks; allergies never made it onto the sheet. You need to take the report seriously, clarify what happened and pass it on before assuming the proposed product is suitable.
question: What should happen before choosing Oskar’s support material?
options: Record the report and check the material.
Ignore reactions involving skin.
Label it severe anaphylaxis without further details.
feedback: The first option keeps the material question actionable. Dismissing skin symptoms loses relevant history; inventing a severe reaction misrepresents the information Oskar provided.
handover: Herr Lind berichtet eine frühere juckende Hautrötung nach Latexkontakt; das damalige Produkt ist unklar. Vor Auswahl der Sprunggelenkversorgung soll das Material geprüft werden; eine schwere Reaktion ist nicht aus der Anamnese belegt.
focus: Bring reported material reactions into the immediate plan

title: Seven means something different today
setting: Nadia rates her knee pain as seven, then lowers the number because she thinks seven might sound dramatic.
hook: Nadia rates her knee pain as seven, then lowers the number because she thinks seven might sound dramatic. Yesterday she used the same number for a headache, and now she worries she has failed the scale. She manages a busy bakery and is accustomed to saying she is fine before anyone asks. You need to explain that the number supports communication rather than proving toughness. Ask what the pain prevents and how it changes, without treating a single score as the complete injury assessment.
question: How can you make Nadia’s pain score more useful?
options: Choose the number for her.
Ask about pain in specific situations without judgement.
Use her calm voice to mark the pain mild.
feedback: The second option captures how the pain behaves. Choosing a number or inferring severity from a calm voice replaces the patient’s experience with an unsupported judgement.
handover: Frau Frank beschreibt Knieschmerzen, die bei Bewegung stärker als im Sitzen seien. Die Schmerzangabe wird situationsbezogen erhoben; aus dem ruhigen Gesprächsverhalten wird kein niedriger Schmerzgrad abgeleitet.
focus: Use pain scales without turning them into a test

title: The job description fits in no checkbox
setting: Yusuf has an ankle injury and asks for a work note.
hook: Yusuf has an ankle injury and asks for a work note. The form offers office work or physical work, but his job combines reception, carrying parcels and standing at a loading door. He laughs that his actual title should be person who gets asked to do everything. You have not yet assessed the ankle. A useful conversation needs the tasks behind the job title and should not promise that sitting work is available simply because a checkbox suggests it exists.
question: What must you learn before discussing Yusuf’s work capacity?
options: Assume reception is always seated.
Promise modified duties on the employer’s behalf.
Describe the real tasks before discussing work capacity.
feedback: The third choice grounds the discussion in Yusuf’s job. The other choices invent either the work demands or an accommodation that has not been confirmed.
handover: Herr Brand beschreibt bei einer Tätigkeit am Empfang zusätzlich regelmäßiges Stehen, Gehen und Pakettragen. Nach Sprunggelenkverletzung ist die individuelle Arbeitsfähigkeit noch zu beurteilen; angepasste Tätigkeiten sind nicht bestätigt.
focus: Clarify actual work demands before discussing restrictions

title: Tell me which part I got wrong
setting: Petra corrects your summary: her knee hit the floor after her ankle turned, not before.
hook: Petra corrects your summary: her knee hit the floor after her ankle turned, not before. She has already told the story twice and sounds tired of being interviewed. You feel the temptation to defend your notes. Her shopping bag is still beside the chair, with a loaf becoming less impressive by the minute. The useful response is a short repair: acknowledge the mistake, restate the sequence and ask whether the revised account is accurate. Accuracy matters more than appearing never to need correction.
question: How should you respond when Petra corrects the injury sequence?
options: Thank her and confirm the corrected sequence.
Defend the first note.
Stop asking because she sounds annoyed.
feedback: The first choice repairs the exact misunderstanding. Defensiveness protects the error; abandoning clarification leaves the mechanism unclear and makes frustration less likely to resolve.
handover: Frau Wolf schildert ein Umknickereignis mit anschließendem Sturz auf das Knie. Eine zunächst umgekehrt dokumentierte Reihenfolge wurde nach Rückfrage korrigiert; Befunde sind noch zu erheben.
focus: Repair a mistaken summary without defensiveness

title: The leaflet that speaks three dialects of medicine
setting: Felix has received an individual ankle-care plan from the treating clinician, but the printed leaflet uses unfamiliar words.
hook: Felix has received an individual ankle-care plan from the treating clinician, but the printed leaflet uses unfamiliar words. He nods through the explanation, then asks whether loading means charging something. The printer has helpfully produced two faint copies and one perfectly dark blank page. Your task is not to invent a new care plan; it is to check what Felix understood from the existing one and identify questions that must return to the clinician before he leaves.
question: What should you do when Felix cannot explain his loading instruction?
options: Repeat the same jargon louder.
Check understanding and clarify the individual instruction.
Create a new loading schedule from memory.
feedback: The second choice keeps the approved plan central while checking comprehension. Repetition without translation leaves the gap; an invented schedule replaces clinical instructions rather than explaining them.
handover: Herr Urban versteht die im individuellen Plan genannte Belastungsvorgabe noch nicht sicher. Die konkrete Anweisung wird vor Verlassen der Einrichtung mit dem Behandlungsteam geklärt; es wurde kein eigenes Belastungsschema ergänzt.
focus: Teach-back of an existing individual plan

title: The form can wait
setting: Noah arrives after a collision and reports pain in several areas.
hook: Noah arrives after a collision and reports pain in several areas. While you begin asking about his medical history, he says he feels increasingly faint. The clinical team is nearby but has not heard this update. You have no reliable vital signs in your notes. This scene is about recognising the limit of a routine language exercise: stop the interview and summon the team immediately. The next useful sentence names the new symptom and the context, not the next box on the form.
question: What takes priority when Noah becomes increasingly faint?
options: Finish the history first.
Call the team now and report the change.
Assume faintness is anxiety.
feedback: The second choice responds to deterioration. Completing routine questions delays assessment, and an anxiety explanation is not supported by the information available in this scene.
handover: Herr Reimann berichtet nach Kollision über Schmerzen an mehreren Stellen und zunehmendes Schwindelgefühl. Die Routineanamnese wurde unterbrochen und das Behandlungsteam sofort gerufen; Vitalparameter liegen hier nicht vor.
focus: Prioritise urgent escalation over a complete interview
topicTitle: Short words in a busy room

title: The missing minutes stay missing
setting: Kian is being assessed by the trauma team after a bicycle collision.
hook: Kian is being assessed by the trauma team after a bicycle collision. He remembers approaching a crossing and then being beside an ambulance, but cannot recall the interval. A companion says he must have been unconscious for ten minutes, although the companion arrived later. You are gathering a short supplementary account while care continues. The task is to preserve the memory gap and the limits of the witness account, not transform a confident estimate into a measured period of unconsciousness.
question: How should Kian’s unwitnessed interval be described?
options: Label the duration unconfirmed and identify the source.
Use the companion’s estimate as a measured fact.
Remove the memory gap because it is uncertain.
feedback: The first choice preserves the clinically relevant uncertainty. The alternatives either invent precision or erase information that the assessing team needs to know.
handover: Herr Herbst berichtet eine Erinnerungslücke zwischen Annäherung an die Kreuzung und Eintreffen beim Rettungswagen. Ein später hinzugekommener Begleiter vermutet Bewusstlosigkeit; deren Auftreten und Dauer sind durch ihn nicht sicher belegt.
focus: Preserve uncertainty around an unwitnessed interval
topicTitle: Short words in a busy room

title: Yesterday is part of today’s story
setting: Rosa reports a blow to her left upper abdomen during a fall yesterday.
hook: Rosa reports a blow to her left upper abdomen during a fall yesterday. The discomfort seemed to ease, but today the pain has increased and she feels faint. She almost booked a routine appointment because the accident was no longer new. You should not let the date make the symptoms sound less urgent. Stop the routine interview and summon the clinical team immediately. Communicate the earlier injury, temporary improvement and current change without declaring a confirmed internal injury from the conversation alone.
question: Does yesterday’s accident make Rosa’s worsening symptoms routine?
options: Book a routine review next week.
Declare a confirmed splenic rupture without assessment.
Call the team now and describe the changing symptoms.
feedback: The third option communicates urgency without inventing a diagnosis. The old event does not make the new symptoms routine, and suspicion is not confirmation.
handover: Frau Stein berichtet nach gestrigem Anprall am linken Oberbauch zunächst Besserung, heute jedoch zunehmende Schmerzen und Schwindel. Die Routineanamnese wurde beendet und sofortige klinische Beurteilung angefordert; eine Organverletzung ist bislang nicht bestätigt.
focus: Communicate a delayed deterioration without premature diagnosis
topicTitle: Short words in a busy room

title: One update, no invented certainty
setting: Miriam is under active trauma assessment.
hook: Miriam is under active trauma assessment. Her brother calls the ward asking whether she will be all right and whether he should cancel a train journey. You are allowed to give him a limited update with Miriam’s agreement, but no final assessment is available. The emotional pressure to offer reassurance is strong. A useful update states what the team is doing, what is not yet known and how another update will be arranged. It does not promise recovery to make a difficult phone call shorter.
question: What can you tell Miriam’s brother while assessment continues?
options: Share all details because he is family.
Give the authorised update and explain what remains unknown.
Guarantee a good outcome to calm him.
feedback: The second choice is useful and bounded. Family relationship alone does not define permission, and a reassuring prediction cannot replace an assessment that has not finished.
handover: Frau Beck befindet sich in laufender Traumaabklärung und erlaubt ihrem Bruder die Mitteilung ihres Aufenthalts und der laufenden Versorgung. Weitere Befunde oder Prognoseaussagen sind für diese Auskunft nicht freigegeben beziehungsweise noch nicht verfügbar.
focus: Give a bounded family update during ongoing assessment
topicTitle: Short words in a busy room

title: The wristband has one wrong digit
setting: Aron notices that his recorded birth date has one wrong digit during a trauma assessment.
hook: Aron notices that his recorded birth date has one wrong digit during a trauma assessment. He is worried that correcting it will slow the team down. The clinical team is continuing urgent care, and you can alert the responsible staff without asking Aron to repeat a long story. This scene concerns identity reconciliation alongside care, not an administrative detour that must finish before treatment. The important communication is brief, specific and directed to someone who can check the identifiers properly.
question: How should Aron’s wrong birth-date digit be addressed during care?
options: Report and verify the discrepancy alongside ongoing care.
Ignore it until discharge.
Stop all care until every form is retyped.
feedback: The first option addresses the error without creating an unnecessary care delay. Ignoring it leaves a mismatch; stopping all care confuses verification with a reason to withhold urgent assessment.
handover: Herr Keller weist während laufender Traumaabklärung auf ein abweichendes Geburtsdatum am Armband hin. Das zuständige Team wurde zur Identitätsprüfung informiert; die dringliche Versorgung wird dadurch nicht unterbrochen.
focus: Raise an identity discrepancy without delaying urgent care
topicTitle: Short words in a busy room

title: Thirty seconds that preserve the essentials
setting: Fiona has arrived after a road collision and the receiving team asks for a brief handover.
hook: Fiona has arrived after a road collision and the receiving team asks for a brief handover. You know the reported mechanism and that she describes chest and abdominal pain. You do not yet know her medicines or allergies. The temptation is to fill silence with a long chronological story or to say no allergies because none were mentioned. Your task is a short, source-aware handover that names the current complaints, identifies missing facts and lets the receiving team continue assessment without waiting for perfect completeness.
question: What belongs in Fiona’s brief handover when medicines are unknown?
options: Fill missing fields with no.
Delay handover until every detail is known.
Hand over the essentials and label unknowns.
feedback: The third option gives the team usable information now. Invented negatives are inaccurate, while delaying the handover can withhold the very details needed for immediate assessment.
handover: Frau Berg berichtet nach Verkehrskollision über Thorax- und Bauchschmerzen. Medikamente und Allergien sind noch nicht sicher erhoben; objektive Befunde werden durch das aufnehmende Team erhoben.
focus: Give concise handover with explicit unknowns
topicTitle: Short words in a busy room

title: Permission in the middle of urgency
setting: Theo is undergoing urgent assessment after a fall.
hook: Theo is undergoing urgent assessment after a fall. A clinician needs to examine his abdomen, and Theo suddenly pulls back because he does not understand what is about to happen. The team remains responsible for urgent care; your communication role is to give a brief explanation and respond to his concern, not launch a lengthy classroom account. You should not treat silence as agreement or promise that the examination cannot hurt. A few clear words can support cooperation while assessment continues.
question: How can you explain Theo’s immediate examination without delaying assessment?
options: Explain briefly and respond to the concern.
Promise there can be no discomfort.
Give a ten-minute lecture while urgent care waits.
feedback: The first choice supports assessment through clear communication. A comfort guarantee is unjustified, while a long lecture puts teaching ahead of the immediate clinical situation.
handover: Herr Mertens äußert vor der abdominalen Untersuchung Verständnisfragen und Sorge vor Schmerzen. Der nächste Schritt wird kurz erläutert; Einverständnis und weiteres Vorgehen werden im Rahmen der dringlichen Versorgung durch das Team geklärt.
focus: Explain an immediate examination briefly and respectfully
topicTitle: Short words in a busy room

title: The patient remembers a different question
setting: Lara is now in a quieter discussion after the acute trauma team has assessed her.
hook: Lara is now in a quieter discussion after the acute trauma team has assessed her. She says she heard the word spleen but cannot remember the rest of the explanation. Her partner has a list of questions, yet Lara first wants to know what the team actually found and what is still being investigated. You do not have the final report in front of you. The task is to arrange a clear explanation from the responsible clinician, not reconstruct results from words overheard in a busy room.
question: How should you answer Lara’s question about the word spleen?
options: Infer the result from the word she remembers.
Review confirmed findings with the responsible clinician.
Tell her the explanation was already given.
feedback: The second option repairs understanding using reliable information. Guessing invents a result, while saying it was already explained ignores the circumstances in which Lara first heard it.
handover: Frau Winter hat nach abgeschlossener akuter Erstbeurteilung Verständnisfragen zu einer erwähnten Milzabklärung. Der endgültige Bericht liegt im Gespräch nicht vor; eine strukturierte Befundbesprechung mit dem verantwortlichen Team wird organisiert.
focus: Repair fragmented understanding after an acute event
topicTitle: Short words in a busy room

title: The pain does not respect the office map
setting: Mara points to her neck and says the pain travels into her right arm.
hook: Mara points to her neck and says the pain travels into her right arm. She works at a desk and has already blamed her chair, her monitor and the colleague who borrowed the good cushion. She asks you to confirm that it is just posture. You have not examined her. The conversation needs a clear map of the symptom: where it starts, where it travels and what other changes she has noticed. An amusing office explanation should not become a diagnosis merely because it sounds familiar.
question: How should you explore Mara’s chair explanation?
options: Confirm the chair is the cause.
Map the symptom and ask about associated changes.
Recommend a new chair without assessment.
feedback: The second option gathers relevant information. The alternatives treat a plausible explanation as a conclusion and move to advice before the symptom pattern has been assessed.
handover: Frau Fink berichtet vom Nacken in den rechten Arm ausstrahlende Schmerzen. Ein Zusammenhang mit dem Arbeitsplatz wird von ihr vermutet; Sensibilität, Kraft und klinische Befunde sind noch zu klären.
focus: Map radiation without confirming the patient’s theory

title: The cupboard was not the whole history
setting: Deniz says his back pain began while lifting a cupboard, then corrects himself: there had been milder discomfort for a week.
hook: Deniz says his back pain began while lifting a cupboard, then corrects himself: there had been milder discomfort for a week. The dramatic lifting moment is easier to remember than the gradual beginning. His family has unanimously promoted the cupboard to chief suspect. You need to separate the first symptom from the later worsening without making Deniz feel caught out. The distinction matters for a clear history, even though it does not by itself establish what is causing the pain.
question: How can you separate Deniz’s first symptoms from the lifting event?
options: Record the first symptom and later worsening separately.
Keep only the dramatic lifting event.
Accuse him of changing his story.
feedback: The first choice preserves the fuller timeline. The other choices either erase relevant context or punish the patient for supplying a more accurate account.
handover: Herr Weber berichtet, bereits etwa eine Woche vor dem Hebeereignis hätten ziehende Rückenschmerzen bestanden; beim Schrankheben sei es zu einer deutlichen Zunahme gekommen. Der Hebevorgang war nach Präzisierung nicht der erstmalige Symptombeginn; die Ursache ist noch ungeklärt.
focus: Separate onset from an aggravating event

title: The awkward question has a reason
setting: Iris has lower back pain and looks puzzled when you ask about bladder and bowel changes.
hook: Iris has lower back pain and looks puzzled when you ask about bladder and bowel changes. She thought she had arrived in the wrong consultation for a moment. Her adult son is sitting nearby and she becomes quiet. No answer has yet been obtained. You need to explain briefly why these questions can matter with back symptoms, offer privacy and ask in plain language. Do not record a negative because the patient hesitates, and do not force sensitive details into a conversation she cannot answer comfortably.
question: What should happen before documenting Iris’s bladder history?
options: Mark normal because she hesitated.
Ask her son to answer for her.
Explain, offer privacy and obtain her own answer.
feedback: The third choice makes an honest answer possible. Neither hesitation nor a companion’s assumptions establishes what Iris is experiencing.
handover: Frau Seifert wird wegen Kreuzschmerzen befragt und wünscht für Fragen zu Blasen-, Darm- und Sensibilitätsveränderungen ein vertrauliches Gespräch. Diese Angaben sind bisher nicht erhoben und werden nicht als unauffällig dokumentiert.
focus: Explain and privately ask sensitive screening questions

title: A new answer changes the priority
setting: Anton reports lower back pain and then says he has newly been unable to pass urine normally.
hook: Anton reports lower back pain and then says he has newly been unable to pass urine normally. He also describes reduced feeling around the area between his legs. He had planned to mention these details only after discussing his work chair. This is a serious change in the conversation. Stop the routine interview and summon the clinical team immediately for emergency assessment. Explain the need for urgent review without declaring a confirmed diagnosis or spending time finishing the nonessential history.
question: What takes priority after Anton reports new urinary and saddle-area symptoms?
options: Call the clinical team immediately and report the new symptoms.
Complete the lifestyle history first.
Reassure him that all back pain is muscular.
feedback: The first choice responds to symptoms requiring emergency assessment. The other choices delay or dismiss the new information without a basis for doing so.
handover: Herr Frey berichtet bei Kreuzschmerzen seit heute über neue Miktionsprobleme und vermindertes Gefühl im Sattelbereich. Die Routineanamnese wurde sofort unterbrochen und das Behandlungsteam zur dringlichen Beurteilung gerufen; eine Diagnose ist noch nicht bestätigt.
focus: Escalate concerning neurological symptoms immediately

title: The report sounds like a demolition notice
setting: Jule brings an old scan report containing the word degeneration.
hook: Jule brings an old scan report containing the word degeneration. She thinks it means her spine is crumbling and asks whether she should stop all movement. She has underlined the word three times with different pens, as if colour might make it less alarming. You have not reviewed the images or her current symptoms. The task is to explain that report terminology needs clinical interpretation and to hear what she fears, not to promise that the old finding explains everything or nothing.
question: How can you address what Jule thinks degeneration means?
options: Confirm that the report means permanent collapse.
Clarify her interpretation and contextualise the report.
Say all scan findings are meaningless.
feedback: The second option makes the report understandable without overstating or dismissing it. Both extreme alternatives claim more than the available assessment supports.
handover: Frau Hartmann ist durch den Begriff Degeneration in einem älteren Befund beunruhigt und erwägt vollständige Bewegungsvermeidung. Der Bericht wurde noch nicht mit den aktuellen Beschwerden und der Untersuchung abgeglichen.
focus: Explore the meaning a patient assigns to a report word

title: The dropped mug is a useful detail
setting: Uwe initially calls his neck problem stiffness.
hook: Uwe initially calls his neck problem stiffness. Later he mentions dropping a mug twice and feeling that his hand is less reliable. He is not sure whether pain, weakness or distraction caused it. His wife has banned the favourite mug from the discussion because it survived and deserves peace. You need to clarify the functional change and arrange clinical assessment, not label a measured weakness that has not been examined or dismiss the report because he can still hold his phone.
question: What does Uwe’s dropped mug justify recording now?
options: Infer normal strength from phone use.
Document definite paralysis.
Clarify the reported change and arrange assessment.
feedback: The third option respects the useful detail and its limits. Phone use is not a full strength examination, while definite paralysis overstates what Uwe reported.
handover: Herr Brandt berichtet bei Nackenbeschwerden über zweimaliges Fallenlassen einer Tasse und ein ungewohnt unsicheres Handgefühl. Beginn und aktuelle Zunahme werden sofort geklärt und eine zeitnahe ärztliche Beurteilung veranlasst; bei neuer oder rasch zunehmender Schwäche ist sofortige Eskalation erforderlich. Eine objektive Kraftprüfung liegt hier nicht vor.
focus: Translate a functional complaint into precise history

title: Back pain has a payroll deadline
setting: Aylin has lower back pain and worries that another absence will threaten her temporary contract.
hook: Aylin has lower back pain and worries that another absence will threaten her temporary contract. When you ask about sleep, she says she lies awake calculating rent rather than simply waking from pain. The two issues have become tangled. You should hear the financial concern without deciding that stress explains the whole condition. A useful history distinguishes pain-related waking, worry and work demands, then connects the appropriate questions to the clinical review. Empathy is not a substitute for assessment, but it makes assessment more accurate.
question: How can you acknowledge Aylin’s stress without dismissing her back symptoms?
options: Separate and acknowledge both pain and worry.
Conclude stress is the diagnosis.
Refuse to discuss work because it is not anatomical.
feedback: The first choice preserves both parts of the history. The other choices either create an unsupported cause or exclude a practical concern that affects the patient’s experience.
handover: Frau Koch berichtet Kreuzschmerzen sowie Schlafstörungen durch Schmerzen und Sorgen um ihr Arbeitsverhältnis. Eine ursächliche Zuordnung der körperlichen Beschwerden zu psychischer Belastung ist bislang nicht erfolgt.
focus: Acknowledge stress without psychologising physical symptoms

title: Yesterday left, today right?
setting: Erik’s referral mentions pain down the left leg, but today he points to the right.
hook: Erik’s referral mentions pain down the left leg, but today he points to the right. He says the earlier note may have been wrong, although he is not entirely sure. The clinic is busy, and copying the old description would be quick. Instead, you need to clarify today’s symptoms, ask about any genuine change and preserve the unresolved discrepancy if necessary. A clean-looking timeline is not worth inventing. The patient should leave the conversation knowing that uncertainty can be documented without anyone being blamed.
question: How should Erik’s right-sided symptoms and left-sided referral be reconciled?
options: Copy the referral unchanged.
Clarify today’s side and flag the uncertain earlier account.
Invent a confirmed switch from left to right.
feedback: The second option distinguishes current information from historical uncertainty. Copying loses today’s report; inventing a switch creates a timeline the patient has not confirmed.
handover: Herr Dorn berichtet aktuell rechtsseitig ins Bein ausstrahlende Schmerzen. Die Überweisung nennt links; ob ein Seitenwechsel oder ein Dokumentationsfehler vorliegt, bleibt nach bisheriger Befragung unklar.
focus: Reconcile changing or conflicting symptom laterality

title: The pain has changed its address
setting: Sofia describes pain that began in her side and later seemed to move towards her groin.
hook: Sofia describes pain that began in her side and later seemed to move towards her groin. She has drawn an arrow on a receipt because pointing feels easier than finding the right medical word. The receipt also contains a shopping list, so the diagram appears beside potatoes and washing powder. You need to use her practical map, clarify timing and associated symptoms, and resist turning a familiar pain pattern into a confirmed stone diagnosis before assessment. Her drawing is a starting point, not a test result.
question: How can Sofia’s drawing help without becoming a diagnosis?
options: Diagnose from the drawing alone.
Clarify the pattern and keep the cause open.
Reject the drawing because it is not medical.
feedback: The second option uses the helpful detail without overstating it. A drawing is neither proof of a diagnosis nor something to discard because it was made on ordinary paper.
handover: Frau Lenz berichtet über seitlich begonnene, später zur Leiste ziehende Schmerzen. Eine Urolithiasis kommt als Möglichkeit in Betracht; weitere Anamnese und Befunde stehen noch aus.
focus: Clarify pain location and migration in plain language

title: The request is for relief, not a quiz
setting: Karim has severe flank pain and asks whether someone can help with it before continuing the long history.
hook: Karim has severe flank pain and asks whether someone can help with it before continuing the long history. He has answered the first questions but struggles to focus. You are practising language, yet he is not there to supply a perfect examination script. The correct response is to alert the treating clinician promptly about the pain and coordinate a brief essential history alongside care. Do not promise that a medicine has already been given or that relief will occur within a particular number of minutes.
question: What should you do when pain prevents Karim from concentrating?
options: Alert the team and shorten the immediate questioning.
Finish every social-history question first.
Promise relief in five minutes without verification.
feedback: The first option responds to the present need. A full routine history can wait, and a timed relief promise invents both treatment knowledge and an outcome.
handover: Herr Seidel berichtet starke Flankenschmerzen und eingeschränkte Konzentrationsfähigkeit im Gespräch. Das Behandlungsteam wird um zeitnahe Schmerzbeurteilung und Versorgung gebeten; eine Medikamentengabe oder Wirkung ist hier nicht bestätigt.
focus: Respond to pain without inventing treatment or relief

title: The side pain has acquired a new warning
setting: Anika came in with pain in her side and urinary discomfort.
hook: Anika came in with pain in her side and urinary discomfort. During the conversation she becomes confused about where she is, and her partner says this is a new change. You do not have a full set of observations. This is not a moment to complete a vocabulary exercise or debate whether the illness began yesterday or the day before. Stop routine questioning and summon the clinical team immediately. State the new confusion and the urinary symptoms clearly, without claiming a confirmed diagnosis from the conversation.
question: What takes priority when Anika becomes newly confused?
options: Finish the symptom checklist.
Assume confusion is embarrassment.
Call the team now and describe the new change.
feedback: The third option responds to a potentially serious change. The other choices delay assessment or attach an unsupported explanation to a new symptom.
handover: Frau West berichtet Flankenschmerzen und Beschwerden beim Wasserlassen; im Gespräch zeigt sie neue örtliche Unsicherheit, die der Partner als ungewohnt beschreibt. Die Routineanamnese wurde beendet und das Behandlungsteam sofort angefordert; Vitalparameter sind hier nicht verfügbar.
focus: Escalate new confusion during an infection-related history

title: Burning is not the same as going often
setting: Timo says he has trouble with water, then looks relieved when you ask what he means.
hook: Timo says he has trouble with water, then looks relieved when you ask what he means. He is not sure whether to describe frequency, burning or the amount. At home he can explain a complicated coffee machine to anyone, but the clinic vocabulary makes a simple bodily function sound like engineering. You need short, separate questions rather than one sentence containing five symptoms. The goal is to discover his actual experience, including what has not yet been answered, without steering him into agreeing with everything.
question: How should you clarify Timo’s vague urinary complaint?
options: Select every urinary symptom on the template.
Clarify each symptom separately.
Ask only whether it is a urinary infection.
feedback: The second option obtains the actual symptoms. A template list invents answers, while asking for a diagnosis requires the patient to supply the conclusion you are still investigating.
handover: Herr Rauch berichtet Brennen beim Wasserlassen. Häufigkeit, Drang und Urinmenge sind noch nicht vollständig erhoben; eine Harnwegsinfektion ist bislang nicht bestätigt.
focus: Split a vague urinary complaint into separate questions

title: The sample pot needs instructions
setting: Greta is handed a urine container and told to provide a middle-stream sample.
hook: Greta is handed a urine container and told to provide a middle-stream sample. She smiles politely but has no idea what the phrase means. The container looks more official than anything in her kitchen, which does not make its purpose self-explanatory. She asks quietly whether she should fill it to the top. Your role is to explain the local collection instructions in everyday language, offer privacy and check understanding. Do not improvise exact amounts or timing when the laboratory instructions have not been checked.
question: How can you explain Greta’s sample request without inventing details?
options: Explain the sequence and confirm local instructions.
Assume the smile means understanding.
Invent a universal collection quantity.
feedback: The first choice makes the task clear and specific. A polite smile is not proof of understanding, and a guessed quantity may not match the requested test.
handover: Frau Dorn benötigt eine verständliche Erklärung zur Mittelstrahlurinprobe. Die konkreten Vorgaben des zuständigen Labors werden erläutert; ein Untersuchungsergebnis liegt noch nicht vor.
focus: Explain a specimen request without embarrassment or invented details

title: Last time is a clue, not a verdict
setting: Henrik had a kidney stone years ago and now calls his new side pain exactly the same thing.
hook: Henrik had a kidney stone years ago and now calls his new side pain exactly the same thing. He has brought an old discharge letter, folded so carefully that the paper seems more experienced than the clinic printer. The earlier episode matters, but today’s symptoms still need their own account. You should ask what feels similar and what is different, review the previous information and avoid allowing a familiar diagnosis to close the conversation before current symptoms and findings are assessed.
question: How should Henrik’s earlier stone affect today’s history?
options: Copy the old diagnosis as confirmed today.
Ignore all previous records.
Use the history while assessing the current episode independently.
feedback: The third choice uses the old information proportionately. Copying it assumes the answer; ignoring it discards relevant context that can inform the new assessment.
handover: Herr Maas berichtet eine frühere Urolithiasis und aktuell erneut seitliche Schmerzen, jedoch mit nach seiner Aussage anderem Verlauf. Der Altbefund wird ergänzend geprüft; die Ursache der aktuellen Beschwerden ist offen.
focus: Use past diagnosis without anchoring on it

title: The result is not for the whole kitchen
setting: Nele takes a follow-up call about a urine test while visiting relatives.
hook: Nele takes a follow-up call about a urine test while visiting relatives. Before you say anything specific, she whispers that the phone is on a shared kitchen table and asks whether you can call later. The family is discussing dinner, not her medical information, but everyone can hear. You need to verify identity and arrange a suitable private conversation, following the service’s process. A result should not be announced merely because the correct telephone number answered, and a rescheduled call needs a clear owner.
question: What should happen before Nele’s results are discussed by phone?
options: Ask a relative to take the result.
Arrange a private, owned callback before details.
Read the result quickly before anyone notices.
feedback: The second choice addresses both privacy and follow-up. Speaking quickly or using a relative does not establish permission to disclose Nele’s health information.
handover: Frau Franke kann beim Rückruf derzeit nicht vertraulich sprechen. Es wurden keine Befunddetails mitgeteilt; ein geeigneter Rückrufweg und die zuständige Person werden geklärt.
focus: Check privacy before discussing a result remotely

title: Who is actually calling whom?
setting: David is told that someone will contact him about pending tests.
hook: David is told that someone will contact him about pending tests. He asks whether that means today, next week or whenever his phone decides to behave. His last appointment ended with the same vague sentence and several days of uncertainty. You cannot invent a laboratory turnaround time. You can clarify the team’s actual follow-up process, who owns the result and what David should do if the expected contact does not happen. The communication task is to turn a passive promise into an agreed route.
question: What turns David’s vague callback promise into a usable plan?
options: Clarify owner, route and fallback.
Promise all results will be normal.
Give an arbitrary deadline to sound organised.
feedback: The first choice creates a usable follow-up plan. A normal-result promise is unsupported; an invented deadline may create new confusion rather than reliable expectations.
handover: Herr Holm fragt nach der Rückmeldung ausstehender Untersuchungen. Zuständigkeit, Kontaktweg und Vorgehen bei ausbleibender Nachricht werden mit dem Behandlungsteam festgelegt; Ergebnisse liegen hier noch nicht vor.
focus: Close a consultation with explicit result ownership

title: CT, MRI and the alphabet soup
setting: Lina has received an appointment letter for a CT scan but calls it an MRI because both involve a machine and an anxious morning.
hook: Lina has received an appointment letter for a CT scan but calls it an MRI because both involve a machine and an anxious morning. Her brother has sent advice for the wrong test. The family chat now has more abbreviations than the hospital letter. You need to confirm the actual requested examination and explain the distinction simply, without describing either scan as a universal answer to every symptom. The immediate practical task is making sure Lina follows the instructions for her own appointment.
question: What should be checked before explaining Lina’s scan preparation?
options: Confirm the requested examination and its own instructions.
Treat CT and MRI as synonyms.
Repeat the brother’s advice without checking.
feedback: The first choice resolves the naming problem before it spreads. The alternatives preserve or amplify a mismatch between the actual appointment and the preparation being discussed.
handover: Frau Peters verwechselt in der Terminbesprechung CT und MRT. Die angeforderte Untersuchung wird anhand der Unterlagen bestätigt, bevor individuelle Vorbereitungshinweise erläutert werden.
focus: Distinguish examination names before explaining preparation

title: The implant card beats a confident guess
setting: Nils is preparing for an MRI and mentions an implanted cardiac device.
hook: Nils is preparing for an MRI and mentions an implanted cardiac device. He cannot recall the model, but thinks it must be suitable because it was inserted recently. His implant card is at home in a folder labelled important things, which has achieved accuracy without convenient location. You need to alert the MRI team and obtain device information for its safety process. Do not assure him that all modern implants are compatible, and do not announce that he can never have MRI based on the word implant alone.
question: How should Nils’s implant compatibility be established?
options: Approve it because the implant is new.
Obtain details for MRI safety review.
Declare all implanted devices permanently incompatible.
feedback: The second option directs the question to the right verification process. Both blanket approval and blanket refusal ignore the specific information needed for a safe decision.
handover: Herr Becker berichtet ein implantiertes kardiales Gerät; Typ und Modell liegen im Gespräch nicht vor. Vor einer MRT-Freigabe werden Geräteunterlagen und die Prüfung durch das MRT-Team benötigt.
focus: Refer implant compatibility to the MRI safety process

title: The tunnel is the real question
setting: Ellen asks how long an MRI lasts, then admits that the real concern is being in an enclosed space.
hook: Ellen asks how long an MRI lasts, then admits that the real concern is being in an enclosed space. She once left a crowded lift and worries she will disappoint the team if she cannot continue. Her carefully packed snack is not the problem today. You need to recognise the anxiety early, discuss it with the MRI team and explain how communication during the scan works. Do not promise that a tablet will remove all fear or dismiss the concern because the machine is familiar to staff.
question: How can Ellen’s specific fear shape MRI preparation?
options: Dismiss the fear as irrational.
Promise sedation will solve everything.
Explore the fear and coordinate support with the MRI team.
feedback: The third choice makes the concern actionable. Dismissal discourages disclosure, while a guaranteed medication solution skips individual assessment and the patient’s actual priorities.
handover: Frau Kraus äußert Angst vor Enge bei geplanter MRT und nennt hörbaren Kontakt als hilfreiche Unterstützung. Das MRT-Team wird zur individuellen Vorbereitung einbezogen; eine bestimmte Medikation oder Wirkung wurde nicht zugesagt.
focus: Explore procedural anxiety before offering solutions

title: The warm feeling and the missing details
setting: Farid says he is allergic to scan dye because he once felt hot during an injection.
hook: Farid says he is allergic to scan dye because he once felt hot during an injection. He cannot remember whether there was a rash, breathing difficulty or any treatment. He is worried the next scan will be cancelled automatically. You need to clarify the prior event and pass it to the imaging team without declaring either a confirmed allergy or a harmless sensation. The useful outcome is a more accurate account of what happened, including the details that remain missing after today’s conversation.
question: What can you conclude from Farid’s recalled warmth after contrast?
options: Clarify and refer the uncertain reaction for review.
Declare it harmless without further history.
Label severe allergy from warmth alone.
feedback: The first choice preserves the event without inventing its cause or severity. The alternatives make opposite but equally unsupported conclusions from an incomplete description.
handover: Herr Lang erinnert ein Wärmegefühl bei früherer Kontrastmittelgabe. Weitere Symptome, Präparat und Behandlung sind unklar; eine allergische Reaktion ist dadurch weder bestätigt noch abschließend beurteilt.
focus: Clarify an uncertain contrast reaction

title: A routine question with a private answer
setting: Mona is attending for an X-ray and becomes quiet when asked about possible pregnancy in front of her colleague.
hook: Mona is attending for an X-ray and becomes quiet when asked about possible pregnancy in front of her colleague. She came directly from work and did not expect a personal conversation at reception. The colleague is only there to help with transport. You need to make the question private, explain that it belongs to the imaging safety discussion and refer the answer to the imaging team. Do not announce a cancellation or approval yourself, and do not treat uncertainty as a negative answer.
question: How should Mona’s uncertain pregnancy answer be obtained and passed on?
options: Ask the colleague to confirm.
Provide privacy and refer the uncertainty to the imaging team.
Treat uncertainty as a definite no.
feedback: The second option protects confidentiality and preserves the information. A colleague cannot establish the answer, and uncertainty is not equivalent to a confirmed negative.
handover: Frau Berg möchte die Frage nach möglicher Schwangerschaft vertraulich beantworten und kann sie aktuell nicht sicher ausschließen. Das Radiologieteam wird vor der Untersuchung zur weiteren Beurteilung informiert.
focus: Ask pregnancy screening privately without deciding the scan yourself

title: Blue on the screen is not a diagnosis
setting: Klara watches coloured areas appear during a vascular ultrasound and assumes blue means something is wrong.
hook: Klara watches coloured areas appear during a vascular ultrasound and assumes blue means something is wrong. She has brought reading glasses so strong that she can inspect every pixel, but not interpret it. The examination is still in progress. Your role is to explain that display colours are part of the technique and need professional interpretation, not give a result from a passing image. Ask what she fears and clarify when the actual findings will be discussed with her.
question: What can you tell Klara about blue areas on the ultrasound screen?
options: Interpret the scan from colour alone.
Tell her not to look or ask questions.
Explain the display and wait for the interpreted findings.
feedback: The third option answers the misunderstanding without pretending to read a complete result. Guessing is inaccurate; silencing questions misses an opportunity to reduce unnecessary fear.
handover: Frau Wendt fragt während einer Gefäßsonographie nach der Bedeutung der Farbdarstellung. Ein abschließend ausgewerteter Befund liegt im Gespräch noch nicht vor; aus der Farbe allein wird keine Diagnose mitgeteilt.
focus: Prevent screen details from becoming premature results

title: The word radioactive needs a calm explanation
setting: Ruben’s appointment letter mentions a radioactive tracer for scintigraphy.
hook: Ruben’s appointment letter mentions a radioactive tracer for scintigraphy. He has imagined a dramatic film scene and wants to know whether he must avoid his grandchildren forever. His concern is sincere even if the image in his head is cinematic. You need to explain the purpose of the tracer in simple terms and direct practical contact, pregnancy or breastfeeding questions to the nuclear medicine team’s specific instructions. Avoid saying there is no radiation or inventing one universal restriction period for every examination.
question: How should Ruben obtain advice about contact after scintigraphy?
options: Clarify the specific tracer-related instructions with the team.
Invent a universal week of isolation.
Say radioactive means no radiation.
feedback: The first choice connects the question to the actual examination. The other answers either create an unnecessary restriction or contradict the meaning of the procedure.
handover: Herr Horn fragt vor geplanter Szintigraphie nach Kontakt zu seinen Enkeln. Die untersuchungs- und substanzbezogenen Verhaltenshinweise werden durch die Nuklearmedizin geklärt; eine pauschale Kontaktfrist wurde nicht genannt.
focus: Explain an alarming term without absolute safety claims

title: The scanner has finished; the answer has not
setting: Elias leaves the scanner and asks the staff member operating it whether everything is normal.
hook: Elias leaves the scanner and asks the staff member operating it whether everything is normal. He has a train booked and wants to phone his partner with good news before boarding. The images have been acquired, but no interpreted report has been discussed. You need to distinguish completion of image collection from completion of medical interpretation. A helpful answer explains the result pathway and checks contact details; it does not infer normality because nobody stopped him on the way out of the room.
question: What does completion of Elias’s scan actually tell you about the result?
options: Infer normality from the quiet room.
Explain the remaining interpretation and follow-up process.
Promise the report before his train without checking.
feedback: The second option explains the real status. Silence is not a result, and a train departure does not establish when specialist interpretation will be available.
handover: Herr Winter fragt nach Abschluss der Bildaufnahme nach dem Ergebnis. Ein ausgewerteter Befund wurde ihm im Gespräch noch nicht mitgeteilt; zuständiges Team und Rückmeldeweg werden geklärt.
focus: Distinguish image acquisition from a reviewed result

title: The stickers are listening
setting: Marvin sees the ECG leads and asks whether the machine will send electricity into his chest.
hook: Marvin sees the ECG leads and asks whether the machine will send electricity into his chest.
